**About the Role:**

As Director of Quality, you’ll lead Helix’s quality department and drive the development of systems, practices, and people to ensure product excellence, regulatory compliance, and customer satisfaction. You’ll hire, train, and manage the team, own the quality system, and make it clear who is responsible for quality at every step.

You’ll report directly to the Chief Executive Officer, partner closely with Engineering, Operations, and our customers to build a proactive, scalable, and right-sized quality system that enables growth.

### **Key Responsibilities:**

**Strategic Leadership & Systems Development**

* Develop and continuously improve a scalable Quality Management System aligned with AS9100 and customer requirements
* Lead departmental strategy, structure, and capital planning to support business growth
* Serve as ISO/AS Management Representative

**Team Leadership & Development**

* Lead and mentor a team of 5+ quality engineers, inspectors, and technicians
* Develop people and build team capabilities in metrology, inspection, and quality engineering
* Foster a culture of collaboration and real-time problem-solving on the shop floor

**Customer & Compliance Management**

* Lead customer and supplier audits; own response and resolution of corrective actions
* Ensure documentation, compliance, and audit readiness
* Build trusted relationships with key customers and act as the face of Quality

**Quality Engineering & Continuous Improvement**

* Partner with operators to implement in-process quality at the machine (not just post-process inspection)
* Drive root cause analysis, SPC implementation, and corrective actions to reduce scrap and improve first-pass yield
* Support new product introductions and ensure proper gauges, fixtures, and inspection plans are in place

**Internal Inspection & Production Support**

* Oversee first-piece, in-process, and final inspection plans
* Continuously simplify and optimize inspection methods to reduce bottlenecks without sacrificing quality

### **What Success Looks Like**

* Promoting Operational Excellence by initiating and helping implement continuous improvement objectives.
* Maintaining a robust QMS system and compliance to AS9100 and ISO 9001 standards.
* Leading the company during customer audits and independent audits towards successful (re)certification.
* Lowering scrap and increasing first pass yield.
* Cross functional collaboration with Production and Engineering to help build quality into the process.
* Implementing solid Corrective Actions to reduce RMAs and DMRs.
* Establishing best practices for the Quality department and the organization as a whole

### **Who You Are**

* A pragmatic quality leader who blends systems thinking with real-world shop floor experience
* Confident navigating between big-picture strategy and hands-on process improvement
* A builder of systems and people, able to lead a team and train on complex equipment
* Comfortable in a customer-facing role and able to communicate clearly with technical and non-technical stakeholders
* Committed to continuous improvement, collaboration, and delivering value across departments

### **Qualifications:**

**Must-Haves**

* 10+ years in manufacturing quality, preferably in machining-based environments
* Strong knowledge of AS9100 and ISO 9001 standards
* Experience leading customer and regulatory audits
* Proven people management skills
* Working knowledge of metrology, CMM, GD&T, and SPC tools
* Experience balancing compliance with operational efficiency

**Nice-to-Haves**

* Mechanical or technical degree
* Experience supporting New Product Development (NPD)
* Six Sigma, Lean, or ASQ certifications (CQE, CQA, CQM)
* Familiarity with vision systems, statistical software (e.g., Minitab), and automation of inspection processes

**About the Company:**

Helix Linear Technologies designs and manufactures high-precision motion control systems for industries where performance matters most, like aerospace, medical devices, and industrial automation. We’re in a phase of strategic growth, investing in R&D, advanced equipment, and new product lines, including aerospace-grade ball screws.

Our clean, climate-controlled facility is built for precision, focus, and continuous improvement. At Helix, you’ll join a team that values ownership, technical excellence, and curiosity.

We offer competitive compensation, comprehensive health, dental, and vision benefits, a retirement savings plan with company match, and paid time off and company holidays.

Helix Linear Technologies is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Due to U.S. export control laws, applicants must be U.S. persons (U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident).

records.title: Senior Director - Customer Experience and Quality
records.description:
Job Overview
 
The Sr. Director, Customer Experience & Quality owns the enterprise-wide direction and execution of Vontier Convenience Retails’ global strategy for customer experience, product quality, and reliability. The role serves as the senior advocate for the customer, this leader establishes global standards, governance, and priorities across global functions. Translating customer feedback, field performance, warranty data, and quality insights into priorities that improve products, services, processes, and support. This leader provides oversight and direction for improving the customer experience and connects Design for Reliability, Supplier Quality Management, Manufacturing Process Control, field quality, and Customer Service & Support into an integrated end-to-end customer experience. Working closely with commercial, product, engineering, procurement, manufacturing, service, and regional leaders, this position drives rapid issue resolution, systemic corrective action, and continuous improvement across the full product life cycle to increase customer satisfaction, loyalty, and business performance.
 
Responsibilities
 

* Own, create, and execute the enterprise-wide global customer experience and quality strategy, setting direction, priorities, and standards, and measurable objectives that advance business objectives, strengthens customer loyalty, and continuously improves customer outcomes.
* Establish and govern a disciplined enterprise voice-of-customer process that integrates customer feedback, complaints, service data, warranty trends, and field performance into product and operational priorities.
* Own and direct the global customer issue management and escalation process, ensuring rapid containment, transparent communication, root-cause resolution, and verification of corrective-action effectiveness.
* Build trusted relationships with strategic customers and customer quality teams; represent the business in quality reviews, escalations, and long-range improvement planning, with accountability for commitments and customer outcomes
* Implement and further develop the Vontier Reliability System to improve product reliability, serviceability, and customer experience across the installed base.
* Develop and lead a multi-year enterprise deployment plan aligned to the customer experience and quality strategy, including performance targets, resources, processes, governance, and organizational capability.
* Collaborate with Product Management, Engineering, Commercial, Service, Procurement, and Manufacturing to embed customer requirements and quality controls from concept through end of life.
* Develop, govern, and continuously improve an integrated enterprise performance system covering customer satisfaction, complaint responsiveness, repeat issues, field reliability, warranty, external PPM, first-pass yield, and cost of poor quality.
* Act as the customer experience and quality advisor to the Vontier Convenience Retail Executive team, using data and customer insights to influence priorities, investment decisions, and accountability.
* Build and lead a high-performing global team and foster a culture of customer focus, collaboration, problem solving, prevention, and continuous improvement.
* Ability to travel up to 30% of working time.

Required Skills / Qualifications / Certifications / Tech Stack
 
Essential
 

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Quality, Business, Operations, or a related discipline.
* 10+ years of experience in quality, engineering, operations, service, or customer facing role within a complex product or manufacturing environment.
* 5+ years of leadership experience with accountability for quality performance, customer outcomes, and cross-functional improvement.
* Demonstrated success leading complex customer escalations, complaint resolution, root-cause analysis, corrective action, and executive-level customer communication.
* In-depth knowledge of quality management systems, product reliability, continuous improvement methods, and standards such as ISO 9001.
* Ability to translate voice-of-customer, field, warranty, and quality data into priorities, measurable action plans, and improved customer outcomes.
* Strong enterprise program change, and organizational leadership skills, with the ability to align global and cross-functional teams around complex business problems, and sustain accountability across functions and regions
* Executive-level communication, influencing, coaching, and relationship-building skills with customers, employees, suppliers, and senior leaders; willingness and ability to travel globally.

Preferable
 

* Advanced technical degree or an MBA is a plus.
* ASQ certification or equivalent (e.g., CMQ/OE, CQE)
* Extensive experience in lean manufacturing; including problem solving and use of kaizen
* Experience working with external partners (suppliers, customers, agencies) to accelerate progress and deliver results.
* Worked directly in or in supporting roles to software development, quality assurance, customer roll-out and software investigation and bug fix resolution.
* Customer facing experience working in roles such as customer service, order management, customer success, application engineering, key account management or sales.

Outcomes and Deliverables
 
Deliverables
 

* Global customer experience and quality strategy with a multi-year deployment plan, clear ownership, resources, governance, capability requirements, and measurable business targets.
* Enterprise voice-of-customer and customer issue management processes, including escalation governance, response standards, root-cause resolution, corrective-action verification, and closed-loop customer communication.
* Integrated customer experience and quality performance system, including dashboards and review routines for customer satisfaction, complaint response, repeat issues, reliability, warranty, external PPM, supplier quality, and cost of poor quality.

Outcomes
 

* A doubling of Net Promoter Scores for “Raving Fans” key customers over a 3 year strategic planning horizon

About Vontier
 
**Vontier (NYSE:** VNT) is a global industrial technology company uniting productivity, automation and multi-energy technologies to meet the needs of a rapidly evolving, more connected mobility ecosystem. Leveraging leading market positions, decades of domain expertise and unparalleled portfolio breadth, Vontier powers the way the world moves – delivering smart, safe and sustainable solutions to our customers and the planet. Vontier has a culture of continuous improvement and innovation worldwide. Additional information about Vontier is available on the Company’s website at www.vontier.com.

records.title: Director of Quality and Education
records.description:
Futures start here. Where first steps, new friendships, and confident learners are born. At KinderCare Learning Companies, the first and only early childhood education provider recognized with the**Gallup Exceptional Workplace Award**, we offer a variety of early education and child care options for families. Whether it’s KinderCare Learning Centers, Champions, or Crème de la Crème, we build confidence for kids, families, and the future we share. And we want you to join us in shaping it—in neighborhoods, at work, and in schools nationwide.

At Crème de la Crème, learning comes alive like nowhere else. Our centers are places that never stand still because kids never do. And when you join us, you’ll become part of that magic—making a memorable impact on young learners and their families every day. In our wow-worthy world of learning, your talents will be the catalyst for creating child care experiences you've never imagined. You’ll link arms with other exceptional humans who care as much about helping kids reach their highest potential as you do—and you’ll know that your work matters.

* As the Crème School Director of Education and Quality, you will 
 + Lead and develop teachers to ensure curriculum alignment with best practices, state standards, and the individual needs of children.
 + Facilitate training and implementation of our comprehensive and developmentally appropriate curriculum for early childhood education.
 + Provide transformative leadership in the field of early childhood education, staying informed about current trends, research, and best practices.
 + Develop a culture of continuous learning and professional development while leading the teaching staff.
 + Establish and maintain high-quality standards for early childhood education program
 + Conduct regular assessments, evaluations, and audits to ensure compliance with Crème standards and licensing requirements
 + Provide guidance and support to teaching staff, promoting a positive and collaborative work environment. In partnership with the Executive Director, host professional development programs to enhance educators' skills and knowledge.
 + Cultivate positive relationships with teachers and parents, involving them in their child's education and development.
 + Collaborate with the community to enhance the educational experience and promote your school within the community.
 + Assist as needed in daily school operations, at times including direct supervision of children
 + Apply data-driven insights to assess program effectiveness, implement strategies to address identified areas of improvement, fostering a culture of continuous quality enhancement.
* Qualifications:
* + Bachelor’s degree in early childhood education, Education Administration, or a related field. (preferred)
 + Meet state specific credentials / guidelines for the role
 + At least one year leadership experience in early childhood education or a related field
 + Proven understanding of early childhood development, educational best practices, and program administration.
 + Excellent communication and interpersonal skills
 + Outstanding customer service skills, strong organizational skills, and multi-task and handle multiple situations optimally.
 + Proven ability to build and sustain positive relationships with diverse staff, families, and community. Commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion in education.
 + Physically able to use a computer with basic proficiency, lift a minimum of 40pounds, and work indoors or outdoors.
 + Able to assume postures in low levels to allow physical and visual contact with children, see and hear well enough to keep children safe, and engage in physical activity.
 + Read, write, understand, and speak English to connect with children and their parents in English.

Range of pay $34,216.00 - $62,100.00 Salary

**Our benefits meet you where you are.** We’re here to help our employees navigate the integration of work and life: 

* Know your whole family is supported with **discounted child care** benefits.

* Breathe easy with **medical, dental, and vision** benefits for your family (and pets, too!).
* Feel supported in your mental health and personal growth with **employee assistance programs.**
* Feel great and thrive with access to **health and wellness programs, paid time off** and **discounts** for work necessities, such as cell phones.
* … and much more.

 
.

We operate research-backed, accredited, and customizable programs in more than 2,000 sites and centers across 40 states and the District of Columbia. As we expand, we’re matching the needs of more and more families, dynamic work environments, and diverse communities from coast to coast. Because we believe every family deserves access to high-quality child care, no matter who they are or where they live. Every day, you’ll help bring this mission to life by building community and delivering exceptional experiences. And if you’re anything like us, you’ll come for the work, and stay for the people.

*KinderCare Learning Companies is an Equal Opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, national origin, age, sex, religion, disability, sexual orientation, marital status, military or veteran status, gender identity or expression, or any other basis protected by local, state, or federal law.*

records.description:
***Metro’s mission is to provide a world-class transportation system that enhances the quality of life for all who live, work, and play within LA County.***

**Description**
---------------

Directs and administers quality management programs in design, construction, and start-up operations of major Metro capital projects. The Director leads Metro’s quality management program for major transit capital projects, overseeing quality during design, construction, testing, and start-up of rail lines, stations, tunnels, and systems. They will also directs a team of agency and consultant quality professionals, oversees contractor quality control programs, and makes sure projects are delivered to standard and ready for safe operation.
 
 
Recruitment Timelines: Interviews are projected to be scheduled for the week of **December 14,** **2026****.** These dates are subject to change. We encourage you to monitor your governmentjobs.com profile and emails for the latest updates.

**Examples of Duties**
----------------------

* Schedules, plans, coordinates, and directs training, certification, team-building, and continuous improvement activities for all construction projects
* Establishes and monitors short- and long-range goals, budgets, schedules, and strategies for quality and continuous improvement programs
* Ensures quality requirements are included in all contracts for services, procurements, and construction
* Reviews and approves consultant/contract personnel/vendor quality programs and qualifications of responsible staff
* Identifies quality problems, then recommends and monitors solutions
* Analyzes and develops appropriate quality staff levels within engineering management and construction management contracts
* Directs the development and implementation of policies and procedures for quality and continuous improvement, including development, implementation, and maintenance of quality program manual; enforces quality program guidelines, standards, and procedures
* Reports to management on quality program performance measures and effectiveness
* Advises staff and management on quality concerns and solutions
* Participates in vendor contract negotiations for consultant and as-needed personnel; negotiates and manages consultant contracts
* Represents Metro with outside agencies and trade and professional organizations
* Authorizes stopping work or shipments that do not meet quality standards
* Supervises, trains, mentors, and motivates assigned staff
* Communicates and implements safety rules, policies, and procedures in support of the agency's safety vision and goals; and maintains accountability for the safety performance of all assigned employees

May be required to perform other related job duties

 

**Minimum Qualifications**
--------------------------

A combination of education and/or experience that provides the required knowledge, skills, and abilities to perform the essential functions of the position. Additional experience, as outlined below, may be substituted for required education on a year-for-year basis. A typical combination includes:
 
 
**Education**

* Bachelor's Degree in Engineering, Construction, Architecture, or a related field; Master's Degree in a related field preferred

**Experience**

* Five years of relevant management-level experience in administering Total Quality Management programs for major capital projects

**Certifications/Licenses/Special Requirements**

* ASQ (American Society of Quality) Certified Manager of Quality/Organizational Excellence preferred
* A valid California Class C Driver License or the ability to utilize an alternative method of transportation when needed to carry out job-related essential functions
* Licensed Professional Engineer (PE) preferred

**Preferred Qualifications**

Preferred Qualifications (PQs) are used to identify relevant knowledge, skills, and abilities (KSAs) as determined by business necessity. These criteria are considered preferred qualifications and are not intended to serve as minimum requirements for the position. PQs will help support selection decisions throughout the recruitment. In addition, applicants who possess these PQs will not automatically be selected.

The following are the preferred qualifications:

* Experience managing quality assurance and quality control programs for the design and construction of rail transit, bored tunnels, underground stations.

* Experience overseeing quality during systems integration, testing, and start-up of rail transit systems, such as traction power, train control, and communications.

* Experience leading quality oversight of contractors on projects delivered through alternative methods, such as Design-Build (DB), Construction Manager/General Contractor (CM/GC), or Public-Private Partnership (P3).

* Experience developing and auditing quality management systems aligned with Federal Transit Administration (FTA) Quality Management System Guidelines or International Organization for Standardization (ISO) 9001.

**Essential Knowledge**
-----------------------

**Knowledge of** (defined as a learned body of information that is required for and applied in the performance of job tasks)

* Theories, principles, and practices of quality management and improvement and standards related to rail design, construction, and start-up operations
* Inspection and materials/systems testing principles and techniques
* Contract negotiation and administration
* Applicable local, state, and federal, laws, rules, and regulations governing requirements and standards of quality management for a public transportation agency
* Modern management theory

**Skill in** (defined as the proficient manual, verbal, or mental utilization of data, people, or things)

* Planning, organizing, and directing the work of quality management functions
* Establishing, implementing, and monitoring short- and long-range goals, budgets, schedules, and strategies for quality and continuous improvement programs
* Determining strategies to achieve goals
* Establishing and implementing relevant policies and procedures
* Analyzing situations, identifying problems, recommending solutions, and evaluating outcomes
* Exercising sound judgement and creativity in making decisions
* Communicating effectively orally and in writing
* Interacting professionally with elected officials, the Board of Directors, and outside representatives
* Mediation and negotiation

**Ability to** (defined as a present competence to perform an observable behavior or produce an observable result)

* Manage sensitive information
* Represent Metro before the public
* Understand, interpret, and apply laws, rules, regulations, policies, procedures, contracts, budgets, and labor/management agreements
* Make financial decisions within a budget
* Plan financial and staffing needs
* Supervise, train, mentor, and motivate assigned staff
* Travel to offsite locations
* Read, write, speak, and understand English

**Special Conditions**

* This job specification is not to be construed as an exhaustive list of duties, responsibilities, or requirements
* The physical demands described are representative of those that must be met by the employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job
* Metro provides reasonable accommodation to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions
* This classification is at-will and the incumbent serves at the pleasure of the hiring authority
* Contributes to ensuring that the Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) policies and programs of Metro are carried out

**Working Conditions**

* Typical office situation
* Close exposure to computer monitors and video screen

**Physical Effort Required**

* Sitting at a desk or table
* Operate a telephone or other telecommunications device and communicate through the medium
* Type and use a keyboard and mouse to perform necessary computer-based functions
* Communicating through speech in the English language required

(AHM)

Metro is an Equal Opportunity Employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, creed, ancestry, national origin, gender, marital status, sexual orientation, religion, age, veteran status, or disability. Learn more about Metro’s Equal Employment Opportunity Program. Metro does not deny participation in the application process to anyone with prior justice system involvement, in line with Fair Chance hiring practices.

 

**Selection Procedure**

Applicants who best meet job-related qualifications will be invited to participate in the examination process that may consist of any combination of written, performance, or oral appraisal to further evaluate job-related experience, knowledge, skills and abilities.

 

**Application Procedure**

To apply, visit Metro's website at www.metro.net and complete an online Employment Application.
 
Computers are available to complete online Employment Applications at the following Metro locations:
 
 
**METRO Headquarters, Employment Office** 
**One Gateway Plaza** 
**Los Angeles, CA 90012** 
**Open: Monday through Friday, 8am-4pm** 
**(Closed Sat & Sun)**

 

**Metro Talent Hub** 
**8501 S. Evermont Place** 
**Los Angeles, CA 90044** 
**Open: Monday through Friday, 9am-5pm** 
**(Closed Sat & Sun)**

**East Los Angeles Customer Center** 
**4501 B Whittier Blvd** 
**Los Angeles, CA 90022** 
**Open: Tuesday through Saturday, 10am to 6pm** 
**(Closed Sun & Mon)**

 

**Wilshire/Vermont Customer Center** 
**3183 Wilshire Blvd, Ste 174** 
**Los Angeles, CA 90010** 
**Open: Monday through Friday, 10am-6pm** 
**(Closed Sat & Sun)**

 

**Rosa Parks Customer Center** 
**Willowbrook/Rosa Parks Station** 
**11720 Wilmington Ave** 
**Los Angeles, CA 90059** 
**Open: Monday through Friday, 6am to 6:30pm** 
**(Closed Sat & Sun)**

 

**Telephone:** (213) 922-6217 or persons with hearing or speech impairments can use California Relay Service 711 to contact Metro.
 
 
**All completed online Employment Applications must be received by 5:00 p.m. on the closing date. Late applications will not be considered.**

* Open to the public and all Metro employees

This job bulletin is not to be construed as an exhaustive list of duties, responsibilities, or requirements. Employees may be required to perform other related job duties.

 

***\*Please refer to the applicable benefit type (Regular or Temporary)\****

**BENEFITS FOR REGULAR EMPLOYEES**

Benefits cover probationary or regular full-time (working at least 40 hrs/week) employees of Metro.
 
 
We offer a range of high-quality medical, dental and vision plan options as well as health care spending accounts for you and your family. Metro will cover a significant portion of your health care premiums.
 
 
**Medical/Dental/Vision Plan** - Employee has the choice of 3 separate medical plans and 3 dental plans. A separate vision plan is included in each medical plan.
 
 
**Group Life Insurance** - PTSC pays for an amount equal to your annual salary, rounded up to the nearest $1,000. Minimum amount of life insurance is $30,000.
 
 
**Accidental Death & Dismemberment Insurance** - PTSC provides $50,000 coverage for each employee. Additional voluntary coverage in amounts up to $500,000 is available at favorable premium rates.
 
 
**Long-Term Disability Insurance** - 100% employer paid. Provides employees with a minimum income of 60% of earnings after six months of disability. Buy up or buy down options available.
 
 
**Holidays** - 12 days a year: New Year's Day, Martin Luther King, Jr. Day, Presidents' Day, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, Veterans' Day, Cesar E Chavez, Juneteenth,Thanksgiving Day, Day After Thanksgiving, and Christmas Day.
 
 
**Time off with Pay (TOWP)** - Compensates employees who are on approved absence from work for reasons such as illness, injury, medical and dental appointments, personal business, vacation, or observance of (a) religious holiday.
 
Years of Service Annual Accrual
 
Hire date - 5 years 20 days
 
Beginning of 6th - 10th year 25 days
 
Beginning of 11th - 15th year 30 days
 
Beginning of 16th + years 35 days
 
 
**Pension Plan** - PTSC retirement plan is the Public Employees' Retirement System (PERS). Vesting is five (5) years. Minimum retirement age is 52, based on the 2% at 62 formula.
 
 
**Other Benefits**: Transportation passes for employees and/or eligible dependents; Medicare; Tuition reimbursement; credit union membership; SDI; Deferred Compensation Plan; 401(K) Thrift plan; EAP; Medical and Dependent Care Flexible Spending Accounts; Flexible work schedules; and Jury Duty Pay.
 

**BENEFITS FOR TEMPORARY EMPLOYEES**

**Temporary (Contingent) employees are eligible for the following benefits only:**

* Kaiser medical insurance
* Public Pension Plan
* 457/401K Plan
* Flex Spending
* Paid Sick Time
* Fare Media
* Rideshare Subsidies
* Metro One Fitness membership

For more information on the Benefits Enrollment for Contingent Employees, please visit LA Metro’s Pension & Benefits website at benefits.metro.net

records.title: Director, Health Access & Quality Operations
records.description:
The American Diabetes Association (ADA) is committed to expanding access to care, advancing health access, improving quality, and achieving better health outcomes for people living with diabetes, prediabetes, and obesity. The Director, Health Access & Quality Operations provides operational and financial oversight for the Health Access & Quality Department, ensuring effective planning, resource management, project execution, and performance accountability. Working closely with department leadership, Finance, Enterprise Strategy, the Program Management Office (PMO), and other internal stakeholders, this position translates departmental priorities into actionable plans, financial analyses, performance dashboards, and executive-level reporting.

 

The Director brings strong expertise in project and portfolio management, financial planning and analysis, dashboard development, and executive communications. The individual must demonstrate the ability to engage directly with Finance leaders on budgeting, forecasting, revenue and expense projections, financial variances, and resource allocation. Equally important is the ability to synthesize complex financial and operational information into meaningful insights, recommendations, and compelling presentations for executive leadership and Board-level audiences.

 

**Responsibilities** 
***Financial Planning & Analysis***

* Lead annual budget development and ongoing forecasting with Finance, including revenue and expense projections, reforecasts and scenario modeling.
* Prepare monthly budget-to-actual reports, analyze variances and recommend corrective actions.
* Track restricted and unrestricted funding, including grants, sponsorships and contracts, to ensure spending is compliant and aligned with funding requirements.
* Develop cost models, cost-benefit analyses and ROI assessments for new initiatives and investments.

 

***Project & Portfolio Management***

* Oversee the department's project portfolio, aligning priorities, resources, timelines and budgets with strategic goals.
* Develop project plans, timelines, risk logs and status reports, and coordinate cross-functional teams to deliver on scope, schedule and budget.
* Partner with the PMO on governance, intake, prioritization and capacity planning.
* Monitor project budgets and burn rates, flagging risks early and proposing ways to reduce them.

 

***Performance Reporting & Executive Communications***

* Build and maintain executive dashboards and KPI scorecards that combine financial, operational and programmatic data.
* Prepare executive presentations, Board materials and management reports that explain complex information clearly.
* Present financial results, forecasts and project status to senior leadership to support decision-making.
* Show how financial investment connects to program outcomes and measurable impact.

 

***Operations & Process Improvement***

* Translate strategic priorities into operating plans with clear owners, timelines and success measures.
* Manage resource allocation, vendor contracts and spending controls in line with ADA policies.
* Identify inefficiencies and lead process improvements that produce measurable results.
* Serve as a trusted advisor to department leadership on financial, operational and project matters.

 

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, Project Management, Operations, or a related field required.
* Formal finance education or training required, demonstrated through a degree, formal coursework, professional certification, or recognized financial management/financial planning and analysis training.
* Formal project management education or training required, demonstrated through a Project Management Professional (PMP) certification, Certified Associate in Project Management (CAPM) certification, or completion of a recognized project management training program.
* Equivalent combinations of education, professional training, and relevant experience may be considered, provided formal training in both finance and project management is demonstrated.
* Minimum of 7 years of progressive experience in business operations, financial planning and analysis, project or portfolio management, or a related discipline.
* Demonstrated experience managing complex projects, developing project plans, coordinating cross-functional teams, and monitoring deliverables and outcomes.
* Substantial experience working directly with Finance leaders or Finance business partners on annual budgeting, revenue and expense forecasting, budget-to-actual analysis, variance reporting, and financial projections.
* Demonstrated ability to interpret financial statements, analyze financial performance, identify trends and variances, and translate findings into actionable recommendations.
* Experience developing and maintaining executive dashboards, KPI scorecards, financial reports, and performance management tools.
* Demonstrated ability to integrate financial, operational, and programmatic data to communicate organizational performance and measurable impact.
* Experience developing executive-level presentations, Board materials, and management reports that communicate complex information clearly and effectively.
* Demonstrated experience engaging senior executives and presenting financial, operational, and performance information to leadership audiences.
* Experience managing multiple projects, priorities, and stakeholders within a complex, matrixed organization.
* Experience identifying operational inefficiencies and implementing process improvements that produce measurable results.

 

***Preferred Qualifications***

* Advanced project management certification or additional specialized training in portfolio management, program management, or business process improvement.
* Experience in nonprofit, healthcare, public health, or mission-driven organizations.
* Experience managing financial performance across multiple programs, funding sources, grants, or geographic markets.
* Familiarity with financial planning and analysis (FP&A), enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems, and business intelligence platforms.
* Experience with Microsoft Project, Smartsheet, or comparable dashboard and project management platforms.
* Experience supporting executive leadership teams and preparing materials for Boards of Directors, Finance Committees, or other governance bodies.

 

**Why Work Here** 
The American Diabetes Association ® (ADA) offers a rewarding career working for one of the premier voluntary health organizations in the world supporting people living with diabetes and/or obesity. Our employees consistently say that our mission, culture, work-life balance, and total rewards package are what they like most about working at the ADA. benefits and our culture:

* Industry competitive base pay. Base offers are determined by several factors including but not limited to your relevant work experience, education, certifications, location, internal pay equity, etc.
* A culture of recognition including new hire welcome announcements, service anniversary awards, referral bonuses, monthly All Employee Assembly, appreciation awards
* Generous Paid Time Off, including holidays, vacation days, personal days and sick days
* Comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental, vision, Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA), disability & life insurance, pet insurance, and retirement savings
* Guided by our mission, we provide full diabetes supply coverage through our medical benefits program
* A company focus on offering mental health programs and work/life balance with most of our employees working remote
* Joining our dedicated team affords the gratification of knowing beyond a doubt that you will impact the lives and well-being of millions

 

**About the Organization** 
The American Diabetes Association ® (ADA) is the nation’s leading voluntary health organization fighting to end diabetes and helping people living with diabetes thrive. Since 1940, we have driven discovery and research to prevent, manage, treat, and ultimately cure diabetes. We advocate for policy changes and improved access to quality care for all people living with diabetes and/or obesity. Through the Obesity Association, a division of the ADA, we are also working to reduce the prevalence of obesity—a leading risk factor for type 2 diabetes.

records.title: Director, Quality and Safety Capability Development
records.description:
**Location:**

Rosedale Office Building

**Department:**

Patient/Medication Safety

**Shift:**

First Shift (United States of America)

**Standard Weekly Hours:**

40

**Summary:**

 

**SCHEDULE:** Monday-Friday, 8a-5p

 

***This role will work onsite at our Rosedale office building in Fort Worth, TX.***

 

The Director, Quality and Safety Capability Development leads the strategy, design, and delivery of organization-wide quality and safety learning programs. This role builds sustainable improvement capability across the health system by equipping leaders, physicians, clinicians, and staff with the knowledge, skills, and tools needed to improve outcomes, strengthen safety culture, reduce variation, and advance continuous improvement. The Director partners across clinical, operational, and administrative functions to support organizational performance and transformation.

 

**Strategy & Leadership**

* Lead the strategic direction for quality and safety capability development across the organization.
* Align education and development initiatives with organizational quality, safety, and performance priorities.
* Partner with executive and physician leaders to identify improvement opportunities and support risk reduction efforts.

**Program Development**

* Design and implement scalable quality and safety learning programs for leaders, clinicians, physicians, and staff.
* Develop curricula focused on continuous improvement, patient safety, leadership effectiveness, and data-informed decision-making.
* Utilize blended learning approaches to increase engagement and application of learning.

**Capability Building**

* Strengthen organizational capability in quality improvement and patient safety methodologies.
* Support leaders and teams in applying improvement science to clinical and operational challenges.
* Promote consistent improvement frameworks, tools, and practices across the health system.

**Leadership Engagement**

* Collaborate with clinical and physician leaders to develop and deliver impactful education.
* Build leader capability to drive quality and safety performance within their areas of responsibility.

**Integration & Measurement**

* Coordinate learning initiatives across departments to create an aligned approach to quality and safety development.
Partner with analytics and operational leaders to measure program effectiveness and organizational impact. 

 

**JOB REQUIREMENTS:**

 

**Experience**

10 years of pediatric healthcare experience including experience in clinical practice, healthcare education, workforce development, professional training, quality improvement, or patient safety. 



**Education**

Master's degree from an accredited college or university in Education, Adult Education, Instructional Design, Health Education, Organizational Development, or a related field. 

 

**Licensure, Registration, and/or Certification**

* Lean Certification or Six Sigma Green Belt required.
Certified Professional in Patient Safety (CPPS) or Certified Professional in Healthcare Quality (CPHQ) required. 

 

**About Us:**

 

Cook Children’s is an equal opportunity employer. As such, Cook Children’s offers equal employment opportunities without regard to race, color, religion, sex, age, national origin, physical or mental disability, pregnancy, protected veteran status, genetic information, or any other protected class in accordance with applicable federal laws. These opportunities include terms, conditions and privileges of employment, including but not limited to hiring, job placement, training, compensation, discipline, advancement and termination.

 

Cook Children’s is a Texas-only employer. If you are hired, you will need to maintain your primary residence within the state of Texas, along with all licenses and credentials required for your position throughout your employment.

CLA seeks an experienced leader to oversee CLA’s Quality Program. Supervise the Quality Assurance Professional, Certified Professional Trainers, Community Case Management Program Manager, RN Association Nurse/CCM Clinical Supervisor, and Shared Living Coordinator, providing supports for people with intellectual and developmental disabilities. The person in this role will review Quality Improvement Systems, monitor and direct audits of service quality and compliance, and act as the steward of policies, conventions, and forms used in Active Treatment. This person will supervise quality and content of training; organize and schedule training, and market training outside of CLA. Research, review, and support compliance with applicable state and federal licensing and program rules, laws, and regulations. As a member of the senior leadership team, the Director of Program Quality will work collaboratively with the Executive Director and peers for the best interest of the entire organization and mission.

​Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in Social or Human Services, Special Education, or related field and 4 years’ experience working with individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities. Progressively more responsible administrative, fiscal, supervisory, and management experience. Proven success in assisted living, health care, or social service setting. Excellent written, interpersonal, verbal communication, and computer skills; ability to prioritize, organize, and manage multiple tasks effectively.

**Skills**

* Healthcare or IDD quality assurance experience, team leadership, and project management experience in healthcare; demonstrated process improvement and compliance management capabilities.

Pay: $75,000.00 - $90,000.00 per year

* 401(k) matching

records.title: Corporate Director of Quality
records.description:
Take the next step with an exciting and growing company
 
As the only fully integrated maker of premium quality wire, rope, and assemblies, Loos & Co holds a leading position in the global aerospace sector.
 
A division of the Central Wire (CWI) Group of Companies encompassing 12 locations in three countries, 750+ employees, and over six decades of excellence, Loos & Co solutions are found in mission critical flight control applications. Our precision-manufactured components are also used for defense, med tech, and heavy industry purposes around the world, in large part because of the people behind our products.
 
Do you have a strong work ethic? Take pride in a job well done? Are you passionate about contributing to individual and team, company and customer successes? If you’re interested in joining a dynamic work environment that offers opportunities to reach your full potential, we want to hear from you.
 
 
Position Summary / Essential Function
 
The Corporate Director of Quality is CWI’s senior enterprise Quality leader and is responsible for establishing and sustaining a culture of quality excellence, accountability, customer focus, product safety, and continuous improvement across aerospace, commercial, medical, metal rope, and assembly facilities. Based in Pomfret Center, Connecticut and reporting to the Chief Operating Officer, the Director leads the enterprise Quality function, develops high-performing teams of Quality professionals, and establishes the governance, systems, standards, metrics, and decision rights required for consistent execution across all locations.
 
A central responsibility of the role is to create a results- and data-driven culture in which decisions are based on objective evidence, process capability, customer and regulatory requirements, risk, and measurable business outcomes. The Director advances the organization from reactive inspection and problem resolution toward prevention, disciplined problem solving, statistical thinking, robust corrective action, and sustained operational excellence.
 
The Director maintains the effectiveness and certification readiness of applicable quality management systems, including AS9100D and ISO 9001 for aviation, space, defense, and commercial operations; ISO 13485 for medical-device operations where applicable; and customer-, product-, and facility-specific requirements for metal rope, wire rope, cable, and assemblies. The role ensures that customer and applicable statutory and regulatory requirements take precedence where they exceed or conflict with general quality-system requirements.
 
Key Responsibilities
 

* Build, lead, develop, and retain a high-performing organization of Quality professionals across CWI, with clear roles, decision rights, measurable objectives, development plans, succession pipelines, and performance expectations.
* Create a results- and data-driven culture of Quality excellence in which teams use objective evidence, trend analysis, statistical methods, and risk-based thinking to identify priorities, prevent defects, and verify sustained improvement.
* Establish and execute the enterprise Quality strategy, organizational design, staffing plan, technical roadmap, and resource priorities in alignment with CWI business and operating objectives.
* Own enterprise governance for quality management systems and maintain certification readiness for applicable aerospace, commercial, medical, metal rope, and assembly facilities, including registrar, customer, regulatory, and internal audits.
* Ensure aerospace quality controls address AS9100D requirements, including operational risk management, configuration management, product safety, counterfeit-parts prevention, special-process control, production process verification, foreign-object damage prevention, traceability, and awareness of ethical behavior.
* Ensure first article inspection and production process verification practices align with AS9102 when contractually applicable, and ensure special processes are qualified, controlled, and approved to customer, regulatory, or other requirements where applicable.
* Ensure medical quality-system controls align with ISO 13485 and applicable regulatory and customer requirements, including risk management, validated processes, traceability, complaint handling, CAPA, change control, and record retention.
* Establish common standards for document and record control, calibration, inspection and test, nonconforming output, CAPA, root-cause analysis, internal auditing, management review, supplier quality, customer complaints, product and process change control, and continuous improvement.
* Establish an enterprise Quality performance-management system with leading and lagging indicators for customer complaints, escapes, first-pass yield, scrap and rework, cost of poor quality, supplier defects, audit findings, process capability, CAPA aging, recurrence, and corrective-action effectiveness.
* Lead monthly operating reviews and formal management reviews that convert Quality data into executive-level insights, identify systemic and emerging risks, assign accountable owners, and track actions through verified closure.
* Develop Quality leaders who can influence Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, and Commercial teams; make risk-based decisions; escalate product-safety or conformity concerns; and hold the organization accountable for results.
* Serve as the senior Quality escalation point for significant customer complaints, product escapes, product-safety events, audit findings, systemic nonconformances, supplier-quality issues, and certification or regulatory risks.
* Ensure robust containment, root-cause analysis, corrective action, effectiveness verification, and lessons-learned deployment for significant or recurring failures, including consideration of human factors where relevant.
* Provide enterprise oversight for supplier-quality strategy, supplier qualification, risk-based surveillance, source inspection, flow-down of customer and regulatory requirements, and supplier corrective action.
* Partner with the Chief Operating Officer, Plant Managers, Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, Commercial, and other leaders to integrate Quality into operational performance, new-product introduction, manufacturing transfers, and change management.
* Communicate Quality-system health, certification status, customer performance, material risks, resource needs, and improvement results clearly to executive leadership and the Board or ownership group when requested.
* Perform other related duties consistent with the role, grade, and business needs.

Required Qualifications
 

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Materials Science, Metallurgy, Quality, Manufacturing, or a closely related technical discipline.
* Twelve or more years of progressive Quality, manufacturing, engineering, or operational leadership experience in regulated or high-reliability manufacturing.
* At least seven years of direct people-leadership experience, including leadership of Quality managers and professionals, performance management, coaching, organizational design, and succession planning.
* At least five years of multi-site or enterprise Quality leadership experience with accountability for common systems, audits, metrics, and cross-site standardization.
* Demonstrated responsibility for an AS9100D-certified quality management system and successful participation as the senior Quality leader in at least one third-party certification or recertification cycle.
* Demonstrated experience with internal and external audit programs, management review, CAPA, root-cause analysis, configuration and change control, supplier quality, product safety, traceability, nonconformance control, and customer complaint resolution.
* Demonstrated use of Quality data and statistical methods to improve performance, including examples of measurable reduction in defects, escapes, cost of poor quality, or recurring corrective actions.
* Ability to travel approximately 25% to 40% to CWI facilities, customer sites, supplier sites, and audit locations, with additional travel during significant launches, audits, or quality events.
* Ability to communicate technical and business risk, priorities, decisions, and performance clearly to plant, functional, customer, registrar, and executive audiences.

Preferred Qualifications
 

* Experience in specialty metals, wire, cable, wire rope, aircraft cable, mechanical cable, swaging, metal assemblies, or other highly engineered metal products.
* Experience leading Quality in aerospace and defense manufacturing, including customer flow-downs, AS9102 first article inspection, source inspection, special processes, counterfeit-parts controls, configuration management, product safety, and foreign-object damage prevention.
* Experience with ISO 13485-certified medical-device manufacturing and risk-management practices aligned with ISO 14971 where applicable.
* Experience with Nadcap-accredited special processes, Defense Contract Management Agency oversight, Federal Aviation Administration-regulated products, or major aerospace prime and Tier 1 customer requirements, as applicable to CWI’s business.
* Advanced degree in Engineering, Operations, Quality, or Business Administration.
* Experience using an electronic QMS, ERP, business-intelligence, and statistical software to manage Quality performance and traceability.

Preferred Certifications
 

* ASQ Certified Manager of Quality/Organizational Excellence (CMQ/OE) or equivalent senior Quality leadership credential.
* ASQ Certified Quality Engineer (CQE), ASQ Certified Quality Auditor (CQA), or AS9100 Lead Auditor certification.
* Lean Six Sigma Black Belt or Master Black Belt.
* Certified Manufacturing Engineer, Professional Engineer, Project Management Professional, or comparable technical credential as relevant.

Key Leadership Competencies
 

* Enterprise Quality leadership and culture building
* Leadership, development, and retention of Quality professionals
* Results orientation and measurable accountability
* Data-driven decision making and statistical thinking
* AS9100D, ISO 9001, and regulated quality-system leadership
* Product safety, compliance, and risk-based judgment
* CAPA, root-cause analysis, and corrective-action effectiveness
* Customer quality and executive escalation
* Cross-functional influence and change leadership
* Continuous improvement and operational excellence
* Executive communication and management review
* Multi-site governance and standardization

Leadership Standard
 
Success in this position is measured not simply by maintaining certifications or passing audits, but by the Director’s ability to build capable Quality leaders and teams, establish measurable accountability, improve the effectiveness of CWI’s quality systems, reduce recurring failures and customer escapes, strengthen process capability, protect product safety and conformity, and demonstrate sustained improvement through objective performance data.
 
Physical and Work Environment Requirements
 
The role operates in office and active manufacturing environments and requires regular interaction with plant operations. It may require walking or standing on production floors, observing machinery and manufacturing activities, using a computer and quality information systems, and communicating in areas where hearing protection or other personal protective equipment is required. Travel among company locations, customer sites, supplier sites, and audit locations is expected. Reasonable accommodations will be considered in accordance with applicable law. This description identifies the essential functions of the position but is not intended to list every physical activity or working condition.
 
Base Salary Range
 
$142,000-$204,500
 
Benefits
 
Subject to the terms, eligibility requirements, and amendment provisions of the applicable plans and policies:
 

* 401(k) with matching
* Dental insurance
* Employee assistance program
* Flexible spending account
* Health insurance
* Health savings account
* Life insurance
* Paid time off
* Referral program
* Tuition reimbursement
* Vision insurance

Pre-Employment Drug Testing

records.description:
**Job Details**
---------------

**Job Title: Director, Quality**

**Location: Meriden, CT**

**Work Arrangement:** Onsite

**About the Role**
------------------

**The Director of Quality** provides leadership, direction, and support to the Quality team, fostering a culture of collaboration, accountability, continuous improvement, and customer focus. This role is responsible for ensuring the safe, compliant, and consistent manufacture, validation, and delivery of chemical products while maintaining the highest standards of quality and operational excellence. As a leader of the Quality Team, the Director coaches, develops, and empowers team members to achieve individual and departmental goals, build technical expertise, and drive continuous improvement across the organization. The Director also ensures timely and effective management of quality-related communications, processes and programs that support both customer satisfaction and business growth. Working closely with colleagues across Manufacturing, Operations, Supply Chain, Regulatory, Sales, and Customer Service, the Director of Quality establishes and maintains robust quality systems, drives regulatory compliance, and identifies opportunities to improve processes, reduce risk, and enhance product integrity. Through strong leadership and partnership, this role helps ensure customer requirements are met, supports the company's commitment to safety and quality, and contributes to the organization's long-term success and reputation in the marketplace.

**Key Responsibilities**
------------------------

* Provide leadership for functional area
* Establish and ensure Quality policies, standards, and objectives ensuring best practices through benchmarking and collaboration with regional and corporate colleagues
* Drive overall compliance ensuring on-time completion of key deliverables
* Responsible for document control, SOP’s, master training schedule, Certificates of Conformance, review and approve relabel PITAs etc.
* Review and approve all quality reports such as annual product review, temperature mapping, validation, internal audit, etc.
* Conducting timely audits, management reviews batch review and release, supply chain, supplier and product qualification
* Advises leadership on quality risks, compliance matters, and strategic quality improvement opportunities
* Driving continuous improvement and risk assessment initiatives
 

**Decision-Making and Problem Solving**

 

* Establishes and approves quality policies, procedures, standards, and quality objectives
* Makes final decisions regarding product release, product disposition, and quality-related exceptions
* Determines appropriate corrective and preventive actions (CAPA) in response to quality events, customer complaints, audit findings, and nonconformances.
* Decides when production processes, materials, or products fail to meet quality or regulatory requirements and may halt production or shipment when necessary
* Evaluates and approves supplier quality programs, qualification processes, and remediation plans
* Recommends investments in quality systems, laboratory capabilities, technology, staffing, and continuous improvement initiatives
* Serves as the organization's lead authority during regulatory inspections, customer audits, and significant quality incidents

**Skills**
----------

* Ability to drive Quality focus throughout the organization
* Strong strategic thinking and problem solving skills
* Experience in developing and maintaining Quality Management Systems
* Expertise in Current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMP)
* Demonstrated ability in leading and managing audits and regulatory inspections
* Strong leadership and decision-making capabilities
* Ability to manage large teams and projects
* Strong communication and influencing skills
* Change management

**Job Requirements**
--------------------

* Bachelor's degree in Chemistry, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Biology, Engineering, Quality Management, or a related scientific discipline required
* Master's degree in a related field preferred
* 7 - 10 years of progressive experience in Quality Assurance, Quality Control, Quality Systems, or Regulatory Compliance within the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, life sciences, or regulated chemical manufacturing industry
* 5+ years of people leadership experience managing and developing professional teams
* Experience leading Quality Management Systems (QMS) within a cGMP-regulated environment
* Demonstrated experience interacting with regulatory agencies, customers, and external auditors

**About Caldic**
----------------

At BrandNu, a Caldic Company, we’re a global leader in distribution solutions, serving diverse markets across the world. Joining us means becoming part of an entrepreneurial, collaborative, and innovation-driven team.

 

**We offer:**

* Competitive benefits including medical, dental, vision, life, legal, 401(k) with company contributions, paid time off and more
* An inclusive, diverse, and dynamic work environment
* The chance to shape the future of specialty ingredient solutions across industries like food, pharma, personal care, and more

We operate in 43 countries around the world. Our innovative solutions are tailored to meet the needs of industries such as food, pharma, personal care, and industrial markets, ensuring sustainable success for all stakeholders. To learn more, visit: www.caldic.com

 

**Ready to Join Us?**

If you're ready to take your career to the next level and join a global leader, apply now at BrandNu Laboratories, a Caldic company!

**Equal Opportunity Employer**
------------------------------

Caldic celebrates diversity and is committed to fostering an inclusive work environment. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, gender, or any other characteristic.

records.description:
### **Activités**

**SUMMARY:**

Reporting to the President, C.E.O., Directs and coordinates activities of personnel at all Hutchinson Sealing Systems facilities engaged in Quality Management System to prevent or eliminate defects in new or existing products or process by performing the following duties personally or through subordinates. This position is designated as a sensitive function for quality, engineering, manufacturing, supplier, audit, compliance, and operational information, including quality performance data, customer requirements, product and process development information, audit findings, corrective actions, supplier performance records, and proprietary company information. The incumbent is responsible for protecting the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information assets in accordance with company policies and customer requirements.

**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:**

Include the following. Other duties may be assigned.

* Analyzes, evaluates, and presents information concerning factors such as quality performance, production capabilities, manufacturing problems, customer quality trends, and quality planning of new products for consideration by other members of the management team.
* Presents and evaluates alternative methods and procedures to establish standardized quality systems based on best practices.
* Participates with other top management personnel in formulating and establishing company policies, operating procedures, and goals.
* Participates in review of product development activities and APQP milestones.
* Conducts Quality System Management review meetings with top management to assess performance and compliance to customer quality requirements.
* Reviews technical problems and procedures of departments and recommends solutions to problems or changes in procedures.
* Confers with engineers and managers about quality assurance of new products and process to improve manufacturing capability.
* Reviews technical publications, articles, and abstracts to stay abreast of technical and quality system developments in industry.
* Travel required on a frequent basis to suppliers and customer facilities as well as other Hutchinson facilities.
* Provides internal quality system audit of Hutchinson Sealing Systems locations.

**EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE:**

Master's degree (M.A.) or equivalent; or four to ten years’ related experience and/or training; or equivalent combination of education and experience.

**QUALIFICATIONS:**

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Qualifications may be waived by management. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

**CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS:**

None.

**SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES:**

Manages subordinates in department. Is responsible for the overall direction, coordination, and evaluation of this unit. Carries out supervisory responsibilities in accordance with the organization's policies and applicable laws. Responsibilities include interviewing, hiring, and training employees; planning, assigning, and directing work; appraising performance; rewarding and disciplining employees; addressing complains and resolving problems.

**TEAM SKILLS:**

Hutchinson is built around teamwork. This position requires the use of good team skills such as cooperation, information sharing, task sharing, timely completion of assignments, good listening and communication skills and overall respect for other team members.

**LANGUAGE SKILLS:**

Ability to read, analyze, and interpret common scientific and technical journals, financial reports, and legal documents. Ability to respond to common inquiries or complaints from customers, regulatory agencies, or members of the business community. Ability to write speeches and articles for publication that conform to prescribed style and format. Ability to effectively present information to top management, public groups and/or boards of directors.

**MATHEMATICAL SKILLS:**

Ability to work with mathematical concepts such as probability and statistical inference, and fundamentals of plane and solid geometry and trigonometry. Ability to apply concepts such as fractions, percentages, ratios, and proportions to practical situations.

**COMPUTER SKILLS:**

Ability to use word processing, spreadsheet applications. Must be familiar with internet research, Microsoft Office software, and the use of e-mail.

**REASONING ABILITY:**

Ability to define problems, collect data, establish facts, and draw valid conclusions. Ability to interpret an extensive variety of technical instructions in mathematical or diagram form and deal with several abstract and concrete variables.

**WORK ENVIRONMENT:**

The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly exposed to moving mechanical parts. The employee is occasionally exposed to fumes or airborne particles; toxic or caustic chemicals. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate.

**PHYSICAL DEMANDS:**

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to walk; sit; use hands to finger, handle, or feel; reach with hands and arms; climb or balance; stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl; and talk or hear. The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 10 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close, vision, distance vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus.

**HEALTH AND SAFETY:**

Must actively support our Health Safety and Environmental policy, immediately report all Safety hazards and correct them when able to safely do so, participate in all required Safety Training, meetings, inspects, and use all required PPE.

records.title: Vice President of Manufacturing
records.description:
**Job Overview**

VP of Manufacturing | Race City Steel

**Location** 
Iron Station, NC

**Reports to** 
VP of Operations and President

About the Role

Race City Steel is hiring a VP of Manufacturing to lead our Iron Station fabrication operation. You’ll manage the fabrication sales and shop floor teams, working directly with the Shop Foreman to improve productivity, quality, and on-time delivery.

Our fabrication shop provides value-added services to Race City Steel’s metal service center locations. The shop handles everything from quick-turn, just-in-time cutting and forming to large, multi-step fabrication orders. You’ll build the processes and capacity to handle both while keeping delivery commitments clear and achievable.

Key Responsibilities

* Lead and develop the fabrication sales and shop floor teams. Set clear expectations for communication, quality, productivity, and follow-through.
* Partner with the Shop Foreman on daily priorities, labor assignments, production scheduling, and bottlenecks. Adjust the schedule as rush orders and customer needs change.
* Coordinate with fabrication sales and branch sales teams to review job requirements, confirm capacity and lead times, and communicate changes before they affect customer commitments.
* Serve as the point of accountability for all machine maintenance, troubleshooting, calibration, and performance. Coordinate preventive maintenance, repairs, and outside service for flat lasers, tube lasers, press brakes, welding equipment, and other fabrication machinery.
* Create and improve processes from quote and order handoff through material staging, production, inspection, and shipping.
* Improve warehouse organization, material flow, and job staging so operators have the material, tooling, and information they need when a job is ready to run.
* Establish consistent quality standards and inspection practices. Address recurring defects and rework with the sales and production teams.
* Track on-time delivery, machine uptime, labor productivity, and rework. Use those measures to identify bottlenecks and follow through on improvements.
* Maintain safe work practices and consistent operating standards across the facility.

Qualifications

* Leadership experience in metal fabrication, manufacturing, or a related industrial operation.
* Working knowledge of laser cutting, tube laser cutting, press brake forming, welding, and related fabrication processes.
* Experience leading shop floor teams and coordinating with sales on job requirements, capacity, and customer delivery dates.
* Experience overseeing equipment maintenance and troubleshooting, including working with technicians and outside service providers.
* Ability to read fabrication drawings, understand job requirements, and build practical processes for a shop with changing priorities.
* Strong communication and organizational skills, with the ability to make decisions and follow through from the sales office to the shop floor.

Pay: $85,800.00 - $120,000.00 per year

Work Location: In person

Daubert Chemical Company is seeking a Vice President of Operations at our specialty chemical plant near Midway airport. The VP leads the functional areas of chemical production, customer service, supply chain, engineering, maintenance and reliability, and EHS. The VP of Operations is a member of the executive team reporting to the CEO, and is accountable for achieving safe, reliable, efficient, and cost-effective operations while consistently meeting product quality standards, customer commitments, and regulatory requirements. This leader will establish clear performance and behavioral expectations, execute with the appropriate sense of urgency, develop organizational capabilities, and drive accountability across all operational functions. 
The successful candidate will balance day-to-day operational execution with long-term strategic planning, continuous improvement and corrective action programs, ensuring that plant equipment, processes, systems, and people are positioned to support business growth and operational excellence. 
This position requires a hands-on, visible leader who demonstrates sound judgment, urgency, follow-up, disciplined problem-solving, and a commitment to improvement and resolution of issues via a methodical corrective action program. The VP of Operations must effectively lead through others, collaborate across departments, and develop sustainable solutions that improve safety, productivity, reliability, product quality, waste reduction, and regulatory compliance. 
 
**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES** include, but not limited to the following.

* Lead, coach, and develop a team of functional managers and operational leaders, establishing clear responsibilities, performance standards, and accountability. Build leadership capability at all levels through coaching, performance feedback, succession planning, and professional development.
* Evaluate organizational structure, staffing levels, technical competencies, and resource requirements to ensure effective operational support.
* Lead operational decision-making with a strong sense of urgency, appropriate prioritization, and consideration of safety, quality, cost, and customer impact.
* Develop and manage departmental operating budgets, control expenditures, evaluate variances, and identify opportunities to improve financial performance.
* Collaborate with Sales, R&D, IT, Procurement, Quality, Finance, and other functions to align operational capabilities with business requirements.
* Provide leadership to production management to optimize plant capacity, equipment utilization, labor resources, product mix, and material availability.
* Develop and ensure execution of a long-range capital investment plan; provide strategic leadership and oversight of plant engineering, equipment performance, reliability initiatives, and capital improvement projects that align with business priorities and integrate safety and environmental considerations.
* Direct the team in the development and effectiveness of preventive, predictive, and corrective maintenance programs.
* Provide executive oversight of EHS programs and ensure compliance with applicable OSHA, EPA, state, local, and other regulatory requirements.
* Support effective safety inspections, regulatory audits, incident investigations, corrective actions, and ongoing risk-reduction initiatives.
* Champion the use of structured problem-solving, root cause analysis, 5S, and other appropriate improvement methodologies.
* Foster a culture of respect, teamwork, ownership, continuous learning, and personal accountability.
* Demonstrate and reinforce the company's Core Values: **Reliable, Improving, Fair, and Caring.**

**SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES**

Directly manages functional leaders. Performs managerial responsibilities in accordance with the organization's policies and applicable laws, such as recruitment, selection, training, goals, performance expectations and accountability, compensation management.

 **QUALIFICATIONS**

* Bachelor's degree in Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or a related technical discipline required; Chemical Engineering strongly preferred. MBA preferred.
* Minimum of 10 years of progressive manufacturing and operations leadership experience, including at least five years leading managers and multiple operational functions.
* Significant leadership experience in specialty chemical manufacturing, batch processing, or a comparable process manufacturing environment strongly preferred.
* Demonstrated responsibility for managing and improving cost optimization with a multi-million-dollar operational budget in manufacturing operations, engineering, maintenance, equipment reliability, capital projects, and resource allocation.
* Experience in a regulated manufacturing environment with strong safety, environmental, and process compliance requirements.
* Proven experience developing and executing operational improvement initiatives with measurable business results.
* Experience leading cross-functional teams and managing competing operational priorities in a manufacturing plant.
* Support change management and transactional integrity within the new ERP, Microsoft Dynamics - D365.
* Expertise in methodologies like Lean or Six Sigma to streamline plant throughput and reduce waste.
* Exhibits solid judgement along with decision making skills.
* Excellent verbal and written communication skills as well as interpersonal, analytical and presentation skills.
* Must read, speak and write English fluently.
* Strong attention to detail with solid organizational and planning skills.
* High degree of professional integrity, ethics and confidentiality.
* Ability to learn company ERP. Requires advances proficiency with MS Office suite i.e. Outlook, Excel, PowerPoint, SharePoint, etc.

**COMPENSATION & BENEFITS**

* Base salary range $209,000-235,000, plus management incentive bonus plan
* BCBS of Illinois Medical & Dental. Vision Service Plan.
* 401(k) Savings Plan + generous company match
* Paid time off with 11 annual Holidays
* Disability, Family, & Military Leave
* Life Insurance, Identity Protection, and more!

Relocation assistance is not available. Must be authorized to work in the U.S.

Daubert Chemical Company is an Equal Opportunity Employer: Disability/Veteran.
