records.title: Chief Manufacturing Engineer-Remote
records.description:
**Fantastic challenges. Amazing opportunities.**
GKN Aerospace is reimagining air travel: going further, faster and greener! Fuelled by great people whose expertise and creativity sets the standards in our industry, we’re inspired by the opportunities to innovate and break boundaries. We’re proud to play a part in protecting the world’s democracies. And we’re committed to putting sustainability at the centre of everything we do, opening up and protecting our planet. With over 16,000 employees across 32 manufacturing sites in 12 countries we serve over 90% of the world’s aircraft and engine manufacturers and achieved sales of £3.6bn in 2025. There are no limits to where you can take your career.
  
  
Role Summary
  
  
As part of GKN Aerospace Airframes E&T, Chief Manufacturing Engineers (CME) lead the development, industrialisation and improvement of Manufacturing Systems whilst serving as the customer-facing representatives of the ME function.
  
  
Day-to-day, a CME is focused on delivery of non-recurring engineering projects including New Product Introductions (NPI), Transfers of Work (ToW), Major Modifications (Mods), Technology Insertions and resolving manufacturing process related quality and delivery challenges together with production engineering teams.
  
  
When necessary, a CME may lead deployed ME resources to deliver these projects, ensuring compliance with identified requirements (e.g. Produceability, Productivity, Cost, Schedule, Regulatory) and adherence to Zero Defect Manufacturing (ZDM) standards.
  
  
**Remote Role**
Travel Requirements
  
  
This is a remote working position that requires frequent routine and occasional non-routine travel (up to 25-50%) to be on-site at GKN facilities and suppliers, including but not limited to; Phoenix (AZ), Wichita (KS), Sumner (WA), Chihuahua (Mexico), Tallassee (AL).
  
  
Candidates must live in a location with strong transport links. This could be 1-2 hours drive (approx.) from a major international hub airport (e.g. Dallas, Atlanta, Houston) or locally to a regional airport with multiple flights per day to major hub airports.
  
  
Role Accountabilities
  
  

* Bids– Accountable to validate and approve the proposed definition of the Manufacturing System and its associated performance targets which are submitted at LG3 (Programme Launch). Working closely with the Industrial Architect, the CME reviews output for technical risks and communicates these to the Programme. This may include process flow, bill of materials, proposed industrial setting, product cost estimates, requirements compliance or technology developments needed. The CME owns the Non-Recurring Engineering cost estimate for the ME technical content delivery.
* NPI– Accountable for delivering a Manufacturing System that fulfils all agreed stakeholder requirements (technical, quality, regulatory), business case metrics and system performance targets between LG3 (Programme Launch) and LG7 (Steady State Production) whilst ensuring that planning, development and commissioning is completed on-schedule and on-cost.
* Sustaining – Accountable for the governance and oversight of a portfolio of Manufacturing Systems, delivered through regular review of system KPIs and Industrial Review assessments. Takes corrective action to ensure Manufacturing Systems continue to perform in-line with the productivity & quality targets set.
* Leadership of Projects- Accountable for delivery of the non-recurring ME activities within a given programme or project. Responsible to provide technical leadership and direction using project management fundamentals: planning & estimating, resourcing & budgeting and reporting on project performance (earned value) to internal business standards.
* Leadership of Teams – Accountable to the Programme and Site for effective utilisation of deployed manufacturing engineering resource while delivering ME content of projects by providing day-to-day coordination, recognition and accountability and implementing ME best practice with the deployed team.
* Quality – Accountable for delivery of manufacturing systems that are Zero Defect Manufacturing (ZDM) capable through a relentless focus on delivering APQP to the AS9145 standard during the NPI phase. Must exhibit and drive a product quality mind-set within ME and ensure compliance to agreed Customer, Regulatory, Business and functional standards.
* Relationships – Accountable to maintain positive and functional working relationships with internal and external customers, to communicate and inform clearly and frequently with key stakeholders within the business, and to foster and champion GKN’s 5 principles within sphere of influence.

**Required**
Role Qualifications
  
  

* Bachelor's degree or equivalent professional qualification in Engineering (Aerospace, Mechanical, Manufacturing, Materials, Electrical, Chemical, or related discipline).
* Minimum of 8 years of experience in aerospace manufacturing or similar, highly regulated environments operating under AS9100 Quality Management Systems.
* Recent experience developing a manufacturing system for a New Product Introduction (NPI) with a comprehensive understanding of product lifecycle gate processes.
* Broad, hands-on experience with common manufacturing processes (e.g. machining, forming, welding, composites, assembly, metrology).
* Knowledgeable of structured problem solving and RCCA methodologies (e.g. 8D) and how to apply these to complex problems.
* Demonstrated capability to organise and drive technical projects to achieve business goals, preferably in complex multi-site environments.
* Ability to lead and influence people, build trust and establish effective working relationships within a global organisation and with external customer stakeholders.
* Fluent in English language, both written and spoken.
* US Person for Export Control purposes

**Preferred**

* Demonstrated deployment of AS9145 APQP process.
* Working knowledge of digital systems for manufacturing (PLM, MES, ERP).
* Deep, expert knowledge in one or more manufacturing process areas (e.g. machining, forming, welding, composites, assembly, metrology).
* Experience working with or for major aerospace OEMs and their systems.
* Proven ability to lead change in a Manufacturing System with evidence of delivering significant improvements in terms of cost, quality or throughput.
* Proven ability to identify and deliver industrial productivity improvements and monitor their efficacy by setting appropriate metrics.
* Project / Programme Management Professional Qualification.
* Six Sigma Certification.

Salary Range
  
  
$120-160k
  
  
We’ll offer you fantastic challenges and amazing opportunities. This is your chance to be part of an organisation that has proven itself to be at the cutting edge of our industry; and is committed to pushing the boundaries even further. And with some of the best training on offer in the industry, who knows how far you can go?
  
  
**A Great Place to work needs a Great Way of Working**
Everyone is welcome to apply to GKN. We believe that we can only achieve our ambitions through a coming together of diverse minds who enjoy collaborating in an inspirational environment. Through our commitment to diversity, inclusion and belonging and by living our five powerful principles we’ve created a culture where everyone feels welcome to contribute. It’s a culture that won us ‘The Best Workplace Culture Award’. By embracing and celebrating what makes us unique we encourage everyone to bring their full self to work.
  
  
We’re also committed to providing an accessible recruitment process, so if you require reasonable adjustments at any stage during our recruitment process please get in touch and let us know.
  
  
We are the place where human dreams, plus human endeavour, shape the future of aerospace innovation and technology.

records.description:
**About Komline**

As a pioneering leader in advanced separation technologies, Komline has established a global reputation for engineering excellence. Through our combination of innovative design, cutting-edge manufacturing capabilities, and decades of industry experience, we consistently deliver the highest quality equipment from our integrated manufacturing facilities. Serving our core markets of Water & Process, Agricultural & Renewables, and Industrials, we pride ourselves on providing comprehensive separation solutions precisely tailored to our clients' requirements. With a strong track record of strategic growth and acquisitions, Komline continues to expand its solution portfolio and technical capabilities while maintaining our commitment to innovation and customer satisfaction.

**This Opportunity**

The Director, Operational Excellence is responsible for building, deploying, and sustaining the Komline Business System (KBS), a consistent operating excellence system across all Komline sites. This leader will partner with Business Unit General Managers, Plant Managers, and functional leaders to improve safety, quality, delivery, cost, working capital, productivity, and overall operating discipline while respecting the P&L accountability of each business. The role will lead Komline’s enterprise continuous improvement (CI) capability, develop CI talent, and ensure proven practices are shared and scaled across the network.

The successful candidate is a hands-on manufacturing leader who combines strong Lean expertise with business judgment, credibility on the shop floor, and the executive presence to influence decentralized business leaders. This leader will be equally comfortable coaching a plant team, challenging a site improvement plan, and communicating enterprise priorities to senior leadership.

Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer, this enterprise-wide role supports all Komline operating sites.

**Responsibilities:**

* Develop and lead implementation of the KBS Operational Excellence strategy, roadmap, standards, and multi-year improvement agenda across all sites

At BlueLinx, our people are at the heart of our success. We are committed to ensuring our team members can build job security, enhance their skills, and make meaningful contributions. We deliver the building blocks to better lives.
  
  
Join us and be part of a company that values its people and strives to make a positive impact on the industry!

* 401(k) with company match
* Tuition reimbursement
* Life Insurance
* Generous Paid Time Off (PTO) and 8 Company Holidays
* Career Growth: Opportunity to develop and advance your career with a leading building products distributor.

**Job Summary**
The Director, Operational Excellence & Business Enablement leads the development and deployment of the BlueLinx operating system across the branch network. This role converts operational strategy, performance data, and technology investments into standard processes, measurable performance improvement, and sustained branch adoption. Reporting to the Sr. Director, Logistics Systems, the Director partners across Regional Operations, Branch Operations, Commercial, Inventory, Finance, Human Resources, Safety, and Information Technology to improve customer service, labor productivity, cost performance, process consistency, and the adoption of new operating capabilities.
  
  
**What You'll Do**

* Understands the company’s vision, mission, and strategy; translates business and functional objectives into clear Operational Excellence priorities and measurable outcomes.
* Leads the enterprise operations performance-management process, including metric definitions, monthly reporting, trend analysis, performance reviews, corrective-action follow-up, and continuous improvement of dashboards and reporting methods.
* Owns governance and continuous improvement for On-Time and In-Full delivery performance, including failure-reason categories, functional ownership, root-cause analysis, corrective actions, and branch adoption.
* Develops and maintains the BlueLinx branch operating system, including standard work, daily and weekly management routines, branch assessment methods, operating playbooks, and sustainment reviews.
* Leads the operational labor-management strategy, including common productivity measures, labor standards, reporting requirements, and branch improvement plans developed in partnership with Regional Operations and Human Resources.
* Serves as the business process and adoption leader for operations, logistics and warehouse technology-enabled improvement initiatives, including transportation, warehouse management, scanning, labeling, automation, data, and artificial intelligence capabilities.

* Working knowledge of warehouse and transportation technology, business intelligence tools, automation, and technology-enabled process improvement.

* Ability to move comfortably between branch-level observation and executive-level decision support.

* Strong follow-through, sound judgment, and a bias toward simple, repeatable solutions that can be sustained by the field.

Our Values
  
  
With every decision and action, we put people first, keep the future in mind, and work as a team toward shared progress.
  
  

* Customer Centric
* Respect
* Collaboration
* Integrity
* Grit

BlueLinx is one of America’s largest distributors of building products, with over 70k branded and private-label SKUs. Headquartered in Marietta, Georgia, we have over 2,000 associates and distribute our comprehensive range of structural and specialty products to approximately 15k national, regional, and local dealers, as well as specialty distributors, national home centers, industrial, and manufactured housing customers.

In this pivotal leadership role you will champion continuous improvement across state government, lead our operational initiatives, and oversee our statewide customer experience program. This position resides within the Office of Administration, the administrative arm of the executive branch, but leads efforts that span all executive agencies to improve service delivery to the citizens of Missouri.

The salary indicated represents a base pay rate. If the individual selected or the position is eligible for a pay differential (e.g., shift, security, or years of service), it will be added to the total compensation in your paycheck. A pay differential does not raise your base pay.
  
  

* Work collaboratively with leadership and teams to encourage, develop, and execute strategies to create a culture of continuous improvement across Missouri state government. Measure the effectiveness of improvements and provide administration with visibility to such improvements.

**Minimum Qualifications**

* Demonstrated advanced knowledge in Lean and Operational Excellence frameworks and facilitation methodologies
* Hands-on experience work with survey, feedback, or data visualization platforms, such as Qualtrics, Tableau, or Power BI

records.title: Head of Quality
records.description:
**About Tutor**
---------------

We believe robots are the biggest lever we have to making the physical world a better, more affordable place. But robots are a rounding error in our society: nearly nine out of ten American factories and warehouses don’t even have a single robot, and robots have yet to make their way into our homes or places of business.

Tutor Intelligence is changing that.

Tutor is a robotics research and deployment company, building generally capable robot hardware and artificial intelligence to enable robots to go where no robots have gone before. Sonny is a semi-humanoid robot with frontier dexterity approaching the human form. Cassie does back-breaking work, moving boxes, pallets, and bulk goods for businesses from family-owned manufacturers to some of the largest brands in the world. Tutor robots are manufactured at scale and operate as a network, combining the whole fleet’s learned experience to train ever more capable robot artificial intelligence.

Founded at MIT and headquartered in Watertown, MA, our team is full stack: we design and manufacture robot hardware, train our own models, work directly with the smallest and largest end-customers, and maintain our fleet across the United States. We’re a team of researchers, engineers, technicians, operators, and sellers who love building things and solving hard problems.

Our mission is grand: robots everywhere, for the common good, raising the standard of living across North America, and then the world.

**The Role**
------------

As Head of Quality, you’ll lead quality as a function, alongside the Head of Manufacturing. The quality engineers and the quality manager report to you, and you’ll grow the team from there. This is a building role: incoming inspection, supplier controls and failure analysis are being put in place now, and you’ll turn them into a system that holds as production grows.

You’ll report to the CTO. As our operations organization grows, you’ll report to its leader. This is an onsite role in Watertown, MA.

**What You'll Own**
-------------------

* The quality system, and the quality targets the company holds itself to
* Supplier quality across our supply base
* Product safety certifications, and a quality record customers and certifying bodies can verify
* The authority to hold any shipment that isn’t right
* Growing the quality team

**Requirements**
----------------

* Led a quality function at a company that builds complex electromechanical hardware in volume
* Built or rebuilt a quality system and taken it through ISO 9001 or an equivalent certification
* Ran supplier quality across a supply base, including overseas suppliers
* Taken a product through product safety certification
* Built and led a team of quality engineers and managers
* Make decisions from data, and hold a shipment when the data says so

**Nice to have:**

* Robotics, automation, vehicles or capital equipment
* Reliability engineering methods: life testing, failure rate analysis, design reviews
* Building quality data and tooling that other teams use
* Experience with manufacturing execution systems

**What to Expect**
------------------

We want you to know exactly what to expect. Here’s what our interview process typically looks like:

* **Recruiter interview:** A conversation with a member of our Recruiting team about your background and what you’re looking for.
* **Hiring manager interview:** A deeper conversation with the hiring manager about the role and your experience.
* **Onsite:** A presentation with the team, 1:1s with key team members, and a tour of our facility.

Some roles include additional steps, such as a technical assessment or take-home exercise. If yours does, we’ll let you know up front. Throughout the process, we’ll aim to keep you updated at each step as quickly as possible.

**Why Tutor?**
--------------

Whether you’re designing robots, closing deals, running deployments, or creating the processes that help us scale, your work doesn’t sit on a shelf. It shows up on real production floors, making physical work safer and more affordable.

Our team of 160+ is driven by curiosity and a genuine love of building. Everyone here takes real ownership, learns fast, and holds a high bar while having each other’s backs. If you love hard problems and creating things that didn’t exist before, you’ll fit right in.

**Benefits**
------------

We take care of our team so they can do their best work. At Tutor, you’ll get:

* Fully employer-covered health insurance, so you’re protected without the premium.
* A managed 401(k) to help you plan for the future.
* Generous time off: unlimited PTO and all federal holidays off for full-time salaried employees, and 16+ days of accrued paid time off plus 1.5x pay on federal holidays for hourly employees.
* Regular in-office meals and team social events throughout the year.

As Tutor grows, so will our benefits. We’re continuing to invest in ways to support our team at work and beyond.

Tutor Intelligence is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes applicants from all backgrounds.

Compensation Range: $220K - $280K

You’ll report to the CTO. This is an onsite role in Watertown, MA.

**What You'll Own**
-------------------

* Scaling production from hundreds of robots a year to many more
* Manufacturing, supply chain, quality, field service and robot operations
* The teams, suppliers and facilities behind production
* A close partnership with engineering

**Requirements**
----------------

* Ran manufacturing or operations at a company that builds complex hardware in volume
* Built an operations function and hired the people who run it
* Been responsible for a fleet of products in the field, including service and support
* Sets clear targets and hires well
* Comfortable on a factory floor

**Nice to have:**

* Robotics, or other products that combine hardware and software
* Experience with contract manufacturers
* Experience with quality systems

**What to Expect**
------------------

We want you to know exactly what to expect. Here’s what our interview process typically looks like:

* **Recruiter interview:** A conversation with a member of our Recruiting team about your background and what you’re looking for.
* **Hiring manager interview:** A deeper conversation with the hiring manager about the role and your experience.
* **Onsite:** A presentation with the team, 1:1s with key team members, and a tour of our facility.

Some roles include additional steps, such as a technical assessment or take-home exercise. If yours does, we’ll let you know up front. Throughout the process, we’ll aim to keep you updated at each step as quickly as possible.

**Why Tutor?**
--------------

Whether you’re designing robots, closing deals, running deployments, or creating the processes that help us scale, your work doesn’t sit on a shelf. It shows up on real production floors, making physical work safer and more affordable.

Our team of 160+ is driven by curiosity and a genuine love of building. Everyone here takes real ownership, learns fast, and holds a high bar while having each other’s backs. If you love hard problems and creating things that didn’t exist before, you’ll fit right in.

**Benefits**
------------

We take care of our team so they can do their best work. At Tutor, you’ll get:

* Fully employer-covered health insurance, so you’re protected without the premium.
* A managed 401(k) to help you plan for the future.
* Generous time off: unlimited PTO and all federal holidays off for full-time salaried employees, and 16+ days of accrued paid time off plus 1.5x pay on federal holidays for hourly employees.
* Regular in-office meals and team social events throughout the year.

As Tutor grows, so will our benefits. We’re continuing to invest in ways to support our team at work and beyond.

Tutor Intelligence is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes applicants from all backgrounds.

Compensation Range: $250K - $350K

Community Health Plan of Imperial Valley (CHPIV) is Imperial County's Medi-Cal managed care plan. We are a locally managed public health care plan committed to working with members, providers, and the residents of Imperial County.

As we continue to build something great, we are looking for a Quality Director to be responsible for the strategic development, implementation, oversight, and continuous improvement of CHPIV's Quality Improvement Program and Performance Improvement initiatives.

**Our next team member will do the following:**

* Direct and oversee CHPIV's Quality Improvement Program and related performance improvement activities.
* Collaborate with the Chief Medical Officer and Health Equity Officer to establish organizational quality and health equity goals, priorities, and strategies.
* Lead initiatives designed to improve clinical outcomes, member experience, preventive health measures, access to care, and care coordination.
* Develop, implement, and monitor quality improvement and health equity work plans.
* Monitor organizational performance measures and identify opportunities for improvement in quality, health outcomes, and equitable access to services.
* Partner with clinical and operational departments to reduce health disparities and improve outcomes among underserved and vulnerable populations.
* Support initiatives addressing social determinants of health, cultural and linguistic needs, and barriers to healthcare access.
* Coordinate quality studies, performance improvement projects, corrective action plans, and follow-up monitoring activities.
* Facilitate Quality Improvement Committee meetings and other quality-related workgroups.
* Develop executive summaries, committee reports, dashboards, presentations, and Board reports regarding quality and health equity performance.
* Support readiness activities and responses related to CMS, DHCS, DMHC, NCQA, and other regulatory requirements.
* Partner with delegated entities, providers, community organizations, and internal stakeholders to improve quality and member outcomes.
* Develop, review, and maintain quality management plans, policies, procedures, annual evaluations, and supporting documentation.
* Monitor project timelines, implementation activities, risks, and barriers to successful program execution.
* Provide leadership, coaching, mentoring, and performance management for assigned staff.
* Promote a culture of continuous quality improvement, accountability, innovation, and health equity.

**You may be right for this job if you have the following:**

* Five (5) years of experience in managed care, healthcare quality, utilization management, care management, population health, compliance, clinical operations, or related healthcare programs.
* Two (2) or more years of program, project, or operational leadership experience supporting quality, regulatory, performance improvement, or healthcare initiatives.
* Three (3) years of progressive leadership, management, or supervisory experience.
* Experience leading quality improvement, clinical operations, regulatory compliance, accreditation, or performance improvement initiatives.
* Experience managing cross-functional projects and organizational initiatives.
* Experience collaborating with physicians, healthcare providers, executive leadership, and multidisciplinary teams.
* Experience developing policies, procedures, reports, presentations, and organizational work plans.
* Experience working within a managed care or healthcare delivery environment.
* Experience analyzing quality, clinical, operational, or regulatory performance data and translating findings into actionable recommendations.
* Knowledge of healthcare quality programs, accreditation standards, and regulatory requirements, including CMS, DHCS, DMHC, and NCQA.
* Experience developing and implementing policies, procedures, corrective action plans, quality initiatives, and operational improvement strategies.
* Strong project management, analytical, problem-solving, and organizational skills.
* Demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively with physicians, executive leadership, providers, health equity leaders, and multidisciplinary teams.
* Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills with the ability to communicate complex concepts to diverse audiences.
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, Word, PowerPoint, and Outlook.

**Our commitment to you:**

* A competitive salary of $130,000-$160,000/ year
* Health, dental and vision insurance for you and your family covered 85%
* Generous paid time off
* A retirement plan with a generous match
* A chance to make a real difference in the Imperial Valley community

Preference will be given to candidates who are local to Imperial, California, but remote candidates living in California will also be considered.

We are an equal-opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

records.title: Director, Production Operations
records.description:
**Sierra Space Careers:**
At Sierra Space, we build the missions and systems that keep our world secure in the domain above Earth.
 
 
Sierra Space team members share a spirit of innovation and collaboration and a belief that we can deliver on the boldest missions in space today. Together with our customers, we aim to safeguard our nation, sustain human presence in space, and secure the freedom of operations in low Earth orbit and beyond.
 
 
Our success is measured by the trust of those who rely on what we build and deliver, and our technologies keep the United States and its allies mission-ready throughout space.
 
 
We are mission-driven, and together, we are an extraordinary team.
 
 
**About The Role**
Sierra Space is scaling from development programs into high-rate, repeatable production across a diversified portfolio of military and commercial systems, including satellites and spacecraft, propulsion systems, solar power systems, and the Dream Chaser spaceplane. As Director, Production Operations based in Madison, Wisconsin, you will play a critical role in executing the production strategy for propulsion development and manufacturing, building the operational systems required to deliver hardware at pace, at quality, and at cost.
 
 
This is an execution-focused leadership role for a proven operations professional with expertise in propulsion systems. Reporting to the Vice President, Production, you will lead manufacturing and assembly operations for propulsion product lines and additional enterprise products within Sierra Space's Madison facility. You will drive standardization of production processes, implement data-driven manufacturing systems, and build high-performing teams capable of scaling propulsion output while maintaining quality and efficiency. You will partner closely with Engineering, Supply Chain, Quality, and Program Management to ensure production readiness and on-time delivery of critical propulsion systems for space and defense applications.
 
 
**About You**
Our mission is driven by an unyielding commitment to advancing space-based technology in service of our customers and safeguarding national security. We seek individuals who are passionate about innovating beyond boundaries and relentlessly pursuing solutions that protect, preserve and empower – to join us in this critical mission.
 
 
We’re looking for team members who align with our values, mission and goals – while also meeting the minimum qualifications below. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.
 
 
**Key Responsibilities**

* Lead manufacturing and assembly operations for propulsion product lines, including day-to-day oversight of production floor activities, scheduling, and workflow management at the Madison, WI facility.
* Execute production strategy to scale propulsion manufacturing from development programs into repeatable, high-rate production with a focus on throughput, yield, and cost efficiency.
* Standardize propulsion production processes and workflows to create consistent, repeatable, high-quality build operations aligned with enterprise-wide best practices.
* Support capacity planning and facility buildout efforts for propulsion manufacturing, including layout optimization, equipment installation, and production line commissioning.
* Drive vertical integration initiatives by standing up and maturing internal propulsion manufacturing capabilities, including additive manufacturing, machining, assembly, and test operations for propulsion components and systems.
* Implement and mature manufacturing execution systems (MES) and production data infrastructure to enable traceability, repeatability, and real-time visibility into propulsion manufacturing performance.
* Establish and maintain production operating rhythm through KPIs, dashboards, and review cadences focused on cycle time, yield, throughput, labor efficiency, on-time delivery, and cost for propulsion production.
* Apply lean manufacturing and continuous improvement methodologies (Lean, Six Sigma) to identify and eliminate production inefficiencies, reduce waste, and improve quality in propulsion operations.
* Collaborate with Propulsion Engineering and Product Assurance to drive design-for-manufacturing (DFM) and design-for-test (DFT) into propulsion product development and support new product introduction (NPI) activities.
* Partner across Supply Chain, Engineering, Quality, Facilities, Security, and Program Management to ensure aligned production readiness, material availability, and execution against propulsion program schedules.
* Manage production budgets for propulsion operations and analyze manufacturing costs to implement cost-saving measures that maintain quality standards and support financial goals.
* Lead and develop production management teams at the Madison facility, including supervisors, engineers, and technicians, fostering collaboration and accountability while upholding company values and a culture of operational excellence.
* Ensure compliance with industry-specific production standards, safety regulations, and quality management systems (ISO, AS9100, GMP, etc.) applicable to aerospace and propulsion manufacturing operations.
* Represent propulsion production operations in cross-functional forums and communicate status, risks, and mitigation plans to executive leadership and external stakeholders, including customers and regulatory bodies.

**Minimum Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in engineering, manufacturing, operations, or a related technical field (or equivalent work experience in lieu of degree).
* 10+ years of experience in manufacturing, production, or operations roles in complex technical industries, with a significant portion in leadership positions.
* The ability to obtain and maintain a Top Secret U.S. Security Clearance is required
* Proven track record of successfully managing large teams and complex production projects in high-rate manufacturing environments.
* Strong background in manufacturing processes, assembly & integration, and operational execution for complex electromechanical or aerospace systems, with emphasis on propulsion systems preferred.
* Demonstrated experience implementing and scaling production operations, including process standardization, workflow optimization, and capacity planning.
* Experience with data-driven manufacturing systems, MES, and production management processes, including OKR development and performance tracking.
* Knowledge of design-for-manufacturing (DFM) principles and ability to collaborate with engineering teams to optimize product designs for production.
* Proven ability to lead multidisciplinary teams and drive operational excellence in fast-paced, highly technical environments.
* Expertise in continuous improvement methodologies (Lean, Six Sigma) with proven ability to identify and eliminate production inefficiencies.
* Strong financial acumen with demonstrated ability to manage production budgets, analyze manufacturing costs, and implement cost-saving measures.
* In-depth knowledge of industry-specific production standards, safety regulations, and quality management systems (ISO, AS9100, GMP, etc.).
* Excellent cross-functional collaboration and communication skills, with the ability to represent production interests effectively to executive leadership and external stakeholders.
* Ability to uphold and model company values while holding others accountable and fostering a culture of operational excellence.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience in propulsion manufacturing and test operations, including liquid or hybrid rocket engines, thrusters, or propulsion subsystems.
* Familiarity with additive manufacturing (3D printing) for propulsion components, including metal printing processes and post-processing.
* Experience in aerospace, defense, satellite, launch, or high-rate hardware manufacturing across both military and commercial product lines.
* Experience with vertically integrated manufacturing capabilities such as propulsion, fluid systems, PCBAs, structures, or integrated vehicle production.
* Experience with spacecraft or satellite integration and production.
* Familiarity with classified manufacturing and secure production operations.
* Experience implementing lean or continuous-improvement frameworks at scale in production environments.
* Experience with automated manufacturing, MES implementation, or production data systems.
* Experience leading organizational change initiatives specific to production environments, including technology implementation, process redesign, and workforce development.
* Experience building and scaling production teams during periods of rapid company growth.
* Master's degree in engineering, operations, business, or a related field.

Compensation:
 
 
Pay Range:
 
 
$164,513.00 - $226,205.00
 
 
Your actual base compensation will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on job-related knowledge and skills, education, experience, internal equity and market competitiveness.
 
 
**IMPORTANT NOTICE:**
This position requires the ability to obtain and maintain a Top Secret U.S. Security Clearance. U.S. Citizenship status is required as this position needs an active U.S. Security Clearance for employment. Non-U.S. Citizens may not be eligible to obtain a security clearance.  The Department of Defense Consolidated Adjudications Facility (DoD CAF), a federal government agency, handles the adjudicative aspects of the security clearance eligibility process for industry applicants. Adjudicative factors which affect the outcome of the eligibility determination include, but are not limited to, allegiance to the U.S., foreign influence, foreign preference, criminal conduct, security violations and illegal drug use.
 
 
**Elevate Your Career**
At Sierra Space, we are committed to your personal and professional development. We empower you to make profound and meaningful contributions and foster a vibrant culture of collaboration, where teamwork ignites breakthrough innovations.
 
 
We also offer a generous benefit package, including medical, dental, and vision plans, 401(k) with 150% match up to 6%, life insurance, 3 weeks paid time off, and more.
 
 
Sierra Space is an industry-leading space and defense technology company providing satellites, spacecraft, and enabling mission systems and components. We deliver mission-proven technologies to our customers that safeguard our nation, protect space-based assets and enable space exploration.
 
 
*Application Deadline: This role will remain posted until a qualified pool of candidates is*
*identified.*
***Please note: Sierra Space does not accept unsolicited resumes from contract agencies or search firms. Any unsolicited resumes submitted to our website or to Sierra Space team members not through our approved vendor list or Talent Acquisition will be considered property of Sierra Space, and we will not be obligated to pay any referral fees.***
Sierra Space Corporation is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to working with and providing reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities. If you need special assistance or a reasonable accommodation related to applying for employment with Sierra Space or at any stage of the recruitment process, please contact us.

records.title: Director of Manufacturing
records.description:
***Custom Fabrication & Assembly Manufacturing | Southeast Alabama***
**Location:**
Dothan, AL (Onsite).
*Relocation assistance is available.*
**Compensation:**
$165,000 to $180,000 base, plus 10% annual bonus
 
 
**Reports to:**
President, Signage Division
 
 
**Team:**
Top leader on site for a custom manufacturing facility with approximately 125 employees across welding, metal fabrication, CNC, forming, electrical, and assembly
 
 
**Required**

* 7+ years of hands-on manufacturing leadership experience with direct responsibility for plant-level performance, whether as a Director of Manufacturing, Plant Manager, Operations Manager, or similar role
* Experience leading a labor-intensive, high-mix, low-volume operation such as a job shop, fabrication, or build-to-order environment. Broad manufacturing judgment matters more than deep expertise in any single process
* A track record of improving throughput, labor efficiency, quality, and on-time delivery through steady, practical improvements while keeping production running
* Working knowledge of manufacturing cost, including labor standards, earned hours or standard costing, and how floor performance shows up in a plant P&L
* Strong floor presence and the ability to earn trust with a long-tenured workforce, build real buy-in, and hold people accountable when the reasons for falling short do not add up
* Experience building repeatable systems and a leadership structure that keep a plant running dependably without relying on any one person
* Resourcefulness and comfort delivering results in a lean environment without large corporate engineering or support teams behind you
* Clear, professional communication with executive and finance leadership, including regular reporting on plant performance
* Bachelor's degree in engineering, operations, business, or a related field preferred; equivalent hands-on manufacturing experience will be considered
* Genuine comfort relocating to and leading in a small Southern community

**Nice to Have**

* Background in custom fabricated products such as signage, store fixtures, displays, architectural metals, or electrical closures
* Industrial engineering training or a similarly technical, process-focused background
* Experience in a private equity-backed or recently acquired manufacturing business
* Lean, Six Sigma, or similar continuous improvement experience applied in a practical, hands-on way
* Experience scaling production capacity, including adding shifts or growing output in a constrained labor market

**The Opportunity**
Our client is a private equity-backed national company that designs, builds, and installs branded products for well-known multi-site businesses across North America. This role leads their primary manufacturing facility in Southeast Alabama, a custom, build-to-order operation where a skilled team works hands-on with aluminum, steel, and electrical components, producing a wide variety of products in small lots.
 
 
The plant has made steady progress in recent years, with lower costs, better quality, and more reliable delivery. The next step is a strong, hands-on leader who can keep that momentum going and take the operation further. This is not a turnaround and not a maintenance role. It is a long-term opportunity to increase output, keep improving cost and efficiency, and build an operation that runs dependably every day.
 
 
**What You'll Do**

* Own plant performance: Lead every aspect of the facility, including safety, quality, throughput, delivery, and cost, with accountability for the plant P&L.
* Lead from the floor: Spend a good part of every day in production, getting to know the people, understanding what drives them, and building the trust that makes change stick.
* Find early wins: In the first 90 days, learn how the factory runs, stabilize performance, and identify practical process changes that make work easier for the people on the floor.
* Drive throughput and cost: Partner with the division President and finance leadership on a multi-year plan to increase output and reduce manufacturing cost, then deliver against it.
* Build repeatable systems: Put processes, metrics, and a leadership structure in place that let the plant run reliably without intensive oversight or dependence on any single person.
* Develop the team: Coach and grow the existing leadership group, including long-tenured leaders who know the product inside and out, and shape the structure the plant needs going forward.
* Hold the line on accountability: Understand the work well enough to see past excuses, set clear expectations, and follow through consistently.

**Why This Role Is Different**
This is the top leadership seat on site. The division President is based in another state, so this person will have real ownership and autonomy over how the plant runs, along with a leadership team that is invested in their success and has done this job before.
 
 
You will not be starting from scratch. The plant has a solid foundation, a clear direction, and the backing of a growing national platform and patient, long-term ownership. The opportunity is to take what has been built and make it better, with room to put your own mark on the operation.
 
 
**The Culture**
The plant has a loyal, tenured workforce that wants to do good work and takes pride in what it builds. The right person brings both process discipline and genuine people skills, someone who can hold the team to a high standard while building the relationships that earn real buy-in. Leadership is not looking for someone to shut things down and start over. They want a steady, visible leader who can find improvements while the work keeps moving, and who will feel at home in a close-knit, small-town Southern community.

**Compensation**
: $175,000 - $215,000 base salary + 15% bonus.

**Benefits**
: Medical, Dental, Vision, STD, LTD, 401k Match 6%, 3 weeks PTO, Tuition Assistance, etc.

**Job Description:**

*Operational Leadership & Plant Management*

* Hold full P&L, safety, quality, delivery, and cost accountability for both rubber manufacturing plants across textile & milling operations including mixing and cord production, acting as a multi-site operations leader.
* Lead, develop, and hold accountable a team of 6-8 managers who in turn lead roughly 200 salaried and hourly employees across multiple shifts.
* Develop and execute annual operating plans, capital plans, and budgets; manage conversion cost, yield, scrap, rework, material variance, and overhead against targets.
* Balance production schedules and capacity across both sites to meet downstream Belt and Hose demand, optimizing changeovers, inventory, and material availability.
* Partner with the VP of Manufacturing, plant managers of downstream operations, supply chain, and commercial teams on demand planning, capacity strategy, and make-versus-buy decisions.
* Spend meaningful time on the floor at each site (approximately 30% travel), maintaining a visible presence on all shifts and engaging directly with operators and supervisors.

*Compound Quality, Technology & Process Control*

* Own end-to-end compound consistency, using rheology (Mooney, MDR/RPA), physical properties, and downstream processing and molding results as the measures of success.
* Reduce process variation through structured methods such as design of experiments (DOE), statistical process control, capability studies, and root cause analysis.
* Develop, standardize, and improve mixing programs (load order, ram pressure, rotor speed, mix time, dump temperature, energy-based and multi-stage mixing) for new and existing compounds, including EPDM, CR, HNBR, NBR, SBR, and NR systems.
* Oversee textile operations (cord unwinding, coating, and rewinding) and raw material handling, heating, and cooling to ensure consistent adhesion and reinforcement performance in finished belts and hoses.
* Lead cross-functional troubleshooting with chemists, the materials lab, process and manufacturing engineers, and downstream operations, leading investigations through disciplined experimentation.
* Establish a single, controlled system of work instructions, batch cards, and process parameters across both sites so that the same compound is produced the same way regardless of site, shift, or operator.
* Evaluate and recommend mixing equipment, automation, weighing/batching, and tooling options for current and new processes and products.

Mill: raw materials are received and handled, then weighed, mixed, heated, and cooled to produce uniform rubber compound for downstream product production.

Textiles: cord is carefully unwound, coated, and rewound to specification, giving finished products consistent strength and adhesion.

*Safety, Compliance & Culture*

* Champion a zero-harm safety culture, including lockout/tagout, machine guarding, mill nip and pinch-point hazards, hot surfaces, combustible dust, and chemical handling.
* Ensure compliance with OSHA, EPA, environmental permitting, SDS requirements, and applicable customer, ISO/IATF, and corporate standards.
* Drive 5S, standardized work, and lean manufacturing practices; treat housekeeping as both a safety and a quality requirement.
* Build a culture of accountability in which following the documented process is the standard and deviations are surfaced openly.

*Talent Development & Organizational Capability*

* Build a bench of operators, leads, supervisors, and managers through structured training, skills matrices, cross-training, and succession planning.
* Set clear expectations, conduct performance reviews, and partner with HR on coaching, corrective action, recognition, and labor relations.
* Capture experienced operators' tribal knowledge and convert it to documented, teachable standards.
* Attract, hire, and retain top technical and operational talent in a competitive labor market.

*Strategy & Continuous Improvement*

* Work with the plant leadership and engineering leadership to define annual improvement initiatives, then align cross-functional teams to targets and track results.
* Lead capital projects, technology transfers, and new-process launches from concept through ramp-up.
* Use KPIs, trend charts, and daily management routines to drive visibility, problem solving, and sustained results.
* Contribute to the North American and global compounding strategy, sharing best practices with sister sites and corporate technology teams.

*Key Performance Indicators*

* Safety: recordable incident rate, near-miss reporting, and audit results
* Compound first-pass quality and out-of-spec rate; rheology capability and variation reduction
* Downstream molding and processing results attributable to compound and cord
* Schedule attainment and on-time delivery to downstream operations
* Scrap, rework, yield, and material and conversion cost versus budget
* Equipment uptime and overall equipment effectiveness (OEE)
* Operator qualification coverage and cross-training depth
* Employee engagement, turnover, and leadership bench strength

**Qualifications Seeking:**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering (Chemical, Polymer, Mechanical, Materials, or Industrial), Chemistry, or a related technical field preferred. Experience in lieu of Bachelors will be considered.
* 8+ years of manufacturing experience, including 5–10 years of hands-on polymer or rubber compounding and mixing experience.
* 5+ years of progressive leadership experience managing managers and multi-shift operations, including responsibility for safety, quality, cost, and delivery.
* Strong working knowledge of internal mixers (tangential and intermeshing), two-roll mills, TSE, weigh-up/batching, and compound testing (Mooney, MDR/RPA, specific gravity, dispersion).
* Demonstrated experience reducing process variation using DOE, SPC, and structured problem-solving methods.
* Proven ability to lead cross-functional troubleshooting with chemists, lab, engineering, and production teams.
* Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills, direct without being abrasive.
* Willingness and ability to travel approximately 30% between sites and to work on the floor in a manufacturing environment.

**Preferred Qualifications (Not Required):**

* Master's degree in Polymer Science, Chemistry, or Engineering, or an MBA.
* Experience in belt, hose, or other engineered rubber product manufacturing, with understanding of rheology and downstream extrusion, calendering, and molding.
* Experience with cord treatment, textile reinforcement, or adhesive systems.
* Experience managing multi-site operations and leading change across sites.
* Lean Six Sigma Black Belt or Green Belt certification, or equivalent.
* Familiarity with ERP/MES systems, mixing control software, and automation for production and material traceability.
* Experience leading capital projects, new-equipment commissioning, or greenfield/expansion launches.

**Core Competencies Seeking:**

* Technical depth: credible expert in rubber chemistry, rheology, and mixing who can coach engineers and operators alike.
* Leadership: develops managers, builds accountability, and engages a unionized or non-union frontline workforce.
* Systems thinking: standardizes work and builds sustainable processes rather than relying on individual heroics.
* Analytical rigor: makes decisions with data, experimentation, and clear trend visibility.
* Business acumen: manages cost, capital, and capacity with a P&L mindset.
* Learning agility: quickly learns new technologies and applies them to business needs.

records.description:
**Job Description**
As the Fort Wayne OEM Director of Manufacturing, you will be a key leadership contributor to the success of the Fort Wayne Manufacturing Hub. Reporting to the Hub Director of Manufacturing, you will provide inspirational leadership in a rapidly growing business and have responsibility for all original equipment manufacturing at the site. This role demands a strategic, results-oriented leader with a proven track record of building and scaling rapidly growing organizations. This means work will be conducted on location at a BAE Systems facility 100% of the time.
 
 
 
 
**Key Responsibilities Include**
**Strategic Product Stream Leadership**

* Own the strategic direction, execution, and performance of the Circuit Card Assembly and Unit Integration factories
* Serve as the primary point of contact between production and program management

**Program Execution**

* Oversee execution of manufacturing in alignment with program schedules
* Ensure all contractual obligations (cost, schedule, performance) are met or exceeded

**Performance Improvement**

* Drive continuous improvement using Lean, Six Sigma Principles
* Implement metrics to monitor production performance
* Initiate corrective actions to resolve production variances, quality escapes, and manufacturing cost variances

**Required Education, Experience, & Skills**

* Bachelor’s degree in Manufacturing, Industrial Technology, Operations Management, or related field; equivalent experience considered OR 20 years manufacturing experience with no degree
* Minimum 10 years’ experience in production/manufacturing
* Minimum 6 years’ experience leading production/manufacturing teams including managing people leaders
* Proficiency with manufacturing management concepts
* Proficiency applying Lean Manufacturing principles and visual management tools

**Preferred Education, Experience, & Skills**

* Proficiency with Oracle ERP
* Formal Lean or Six Sigma training/certification
* Minimum 10 years’ experience leading people leaders of production/manufacturing teams

**Pay Information**
Full-Time Salary Range: $153377 - $260743
 
 
Please note: This range is based on our market pay structures. However, individual salaries are determined by a variety of factors including, but not limited to: business considerations, local market conditions, and internal equity, as well as candidate qualifications, such as skills, education, and experience.
 
 
Employee Benefits: At BAE Systems, we support our employees in all aspects of their life, including their health and financial well-being. Regular employees scheduled to work 20+ hours per week are offered: health, dental, and vision insurance; health savings accounts; a 401(k) savings plan; disability coverage; and life and accident insurance. We also have an employee assistance program, a legal plan, and other perks including discounts on things like home, auto, and pet insurance. Our leave programs include paid time off, paid holidays, as well as other types of leave, including paid parental, military, bereavement, and any applicable federal and state sick leave. Employees may participate in the company recognition program to receive monetary or non-monetary recognition awards. Other incentives may be available based on position level and/or job specifics.
 
 
 
 
**About BAE Systems, Inc.**
BAE Systems, Inc. is a defense, aerospace, and security company headquartered in Falls Church, Virginia, with more than 40,000 employees worldwide. We serve, supply, and protect those who protect us. As one of the most geographically diverse international defense companies, we deliver a full range of products and services spanning air, land, maritime, space, and cyber, including advanced electronics, intelligence solutions, and dedicated customer support.
 
 
Our culture is performance-driven and values-led, built on curiosity, creativity, and collaboration. Purpose isn't a tagline here. It's what drives us. We're developing breakthrough technologies that defend national security and make a lasting impact on our communities and our planet. When you join BAE Systems, you're not just building a career. You're contributing to a mission that truly matters.

records.description:
**Job Description**
Executive Manufacturing Leadership Opportunity
 
 
BASX is seeking a transformational manufacturing executive to lead one of its key operations as Site Leader (Director of Manufacturing).
 
 
This role is far more than manufacturing oversight. It is an opportunity to shape the future of a growing operation, influence enterprise strategy, drive large-scale operational transformation, and build the manufacturing capabilities required to support long-term business growth.
 
 
As the senior manufacturing leader for the site, you will serve as a trusted business partner to executive leadership and will be responsible for aligning manufacturing strategy, operational performance, capital investment, workforce development, and technology advancement with the organization's strategic objectives.
 
 
The successful candidate will bring a balance of strategic vision and operational discipline while building a culture of accountability, innovation, continuous improvement, and sustainable growth.
 
 
**This Is a Unique Opportunity To**




+ Lead manufacturing operations that directly support the growth strategy of a rapidly expanding organization.
+ Shape the future-state manufacturing vision through automation, digital transformation, and Industry 4.0 initiatives.
+ Influence major capital investment decisions, facility expansion plans, and manufacturing technology roadmaps.
+ Build leadership capability and strengthen organizational effectiveness across the operation.
+ Partner directly with executive leadership to establish long-term operational strategies.
+ Drive measurable improvements in productivity, quality, safety, delivery performance, and profitability.
+ Leave a lasting legacy by creating a scalable manufacturing organization positioned for future growth.

**What You'll Accomplish**
**Enterprise Impact**




+ Establish and execute a multi-year manufacturing strategy aligned with company growth initiatives.
+ Lead initiatives that enhance operational scalability, profitability, and customer satisfaction.
+ Drive business performance through operational excellence, capacity optimization, and strategic planning.

**Manufacturing Transformation**




+ Lead cultural and operational transformation initiatives across the facility.
+ Advance Lean Manufacturing and Continuous Improvement principles throughout the organization.
+ Champion automation, smart factory technologies, and digital manufacturing capabilities.
+ Identify and implement breakthrough improvements that create sustainable competitive advantages.

**Executive Partnership**




+ Serve as a key member of the site leadership team.
+ Collaborate with executive leadership on strategic business decisions.
+ Influence organizational direction through data-driven decision-making and operational expertise.
+ Provide strategic recommendations regarding investments, growth opportunities, risk mitigation, and resource allocation.

**Leadership Development**




+ Build and mentor a high-performing leadership team.
+ Create succession plans and strengthen organizational capability.
+ Foster a culture focused on accountability, engagement, innovation, and results.
+ Attract and retain top manufacturing talent.

**Scope & Organizational Impact**
Serves as the senior manufacturing leader for BASX's Redmond operation, directing a workforce of more than 500 employees across a manufacturing footprint exceeding 300,000 square feet. Responsible for shaping manufacturing strategy, leading operational transformation, guiding capital investments, and building the organizational capabilities required to support continued growth and market leadership.
 
 
**The Executive Profile**
We are seeking a respected manufacturing leader with a demonstrated history of transforming operations, developing talent, and delivering measurable business results.
 
 
**The Ideal Candidate Must Have**




+ Proven experience leading large-scale manufacturing organizations.
+ Demonstrated success driving operational and cultural transformation.
+ Experience leading automation, digital manufacturing, or Industry 4.0 initiatives.
+ Strong financial acumen with experience managing capital investments and operating budgets.
+ A track record of improving productivity, quality, throughput, and operational efficiency.
+ Exceptional leadership presence and executive communication skills.
+ The ability to balance strategic vision with executional excellence.
+ Experience building high-performing leadership teams and scalable organizational structures.

**Preferred Leadership Competencies**
**Strategic Leadership**




+ Manufacturing Transformation
+ Business Transformation
+ Enterprise Leadership
+ Strategic Planning
+ Organizational Development

**Operational Excellence**




+ Lean Manufacturing
+ Six Sigma
+ Continuous Improvement
+ Operational Excellence
+ Value Stream Optimization

**Innovation & Growth**




+ Industry 4.0
+ Smart Factory Strategy
+ Digital Manufacturing
+ Manufacturing Innovation
+ Automation Strategy

**Financial & Capital Management**




+ Capital Projects
+ Capacity Planning
+ Facility Expansion
+ Cost Optimization
+ Investment Planning

**Education And Experience Requirements**
Requires a four-year ABET-accredited degree in engineering with significant experience in manufacturing technology; 10+ years of experience in manufacturing operations, including leadership of large-scale initiatives; or any combination of education and experience, which would provide an equivalent background. Advanced degrees and certifications in quality control or advanced manufacturing are preferred.
 
 
**Why BASX?**
BASX continues to invest in advanced manufacturing capabilities, growth initiatives, and operational excellence. This position offers the opportunity to lead meaningful change within an organization committed to innovation, customer success, and long-term growth.
 
 
For leaders who enjoy building organizations, developing talent, optimizing operations, and shaping strategy, this role offers both the challenge and visibility necessary to make a significant impact.
 
 
**Why Redmond, Oregon?**
Located in the heart of Central Oregon, Redmond offers an exceptional quality of life and access to world-class outdoor recreation.
 
 
**Lifestyle Advantages**




+ Hiking, skiing, fishing, mountain biking, golf, and year-round outdoor activities
+ Family-friendly communities and excellent schools
+ One of the fastest-growing regions in the Pacific Northwest
+ No Oregon state sales tax
+ Easy access to Bend, the Cascade Mountains, and major regional airports

**Additional Benefits**




+ Executive-level compensation package
+ Annual incentive opportunity
+ Comprehensive benefits program
+ Relocation assistance available
+ Sponsorship not available

**Build Something That Lasts**
If you are a forward-thinking manufacturing executive who thrives on creating organizational capability, driving transformation, and delivering business results, this is an opportunity to lead at a strategic level while shaping the future of a growing operation.
 
 
**Mental And Physical Functions**
This role requires strategic thinking, technical leadership, and the ability to manage complex initiatives across departments and locations. The Director must be capable of balancing high-level planning with hands-on engagement in manufacturing operations.
 
 

* Communicates effectively in written and spoken form
* Possesses excellent interpersonal and leadership skills
* Demonstrates strong organizational and multitasking abilities
* Works effectively in a fast-paced, high-pressure environment
* Ability to lift up to 50 lbs.
* Sit or stand for up to 95% of work hours
* Regular visits to manufacturing facilities with exposure to seasonal hot and cold temperatures, dust, and chemical fumes

**Work Environment**
The Director, Manufacturing operates in both office and production environments, with frequent interaction across departments and facilities.
 
 

* Work is performed in a combination of office and factory settings
* Exposure to loud noise, dust, temperature fluctuations, and industrial equipment
* Use of personal protective equipment (PPE) is required when on the production floor
* Frequent collaboration with engineering, operations, quality, and executive leadership teams
* This position is designated as a safety-sensitive role and is subject to drug and alcohol testing, including random testing
* Compliance with all company safety and operational policies is mandatory

**Disclaimer**
Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities and activities may change at a time with or without notice. This job description is not an exhaustive list of all functions that the employee may be required to perform, and the employee may be required to perform additional functions. The company reserves the right to revise this job description at any time. The employee must be able to perform the essential functions of the position satisfactorily. If requested, reasonable accommodations may be made to enable employees with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the job, absent undue hardship.
 
 
#BASX
 
 
**Benefits And Compensation Summary**
We take care of our people. We offer competitive compensation and robust benefits to all full-time team members, including:
 
 

* Tuition reimbursement
* Paid time-off
* Paid holidays
* Healthcare insurance & Health Savings Accounts
* Profit sharing or Annual Incentive Plan Bonus
* Premium 401(k) plan

records.description:
**Title:**
Plant Manager
 
 
**Company:**
Manufacturing Group
 
 
**Location:**
Tewksbury, MA area
 
 
**Reports to:**
CEO
 
 
**Direct reports:**
Production, Maintenance, Sanitation, and Warehouse/Shipping leaders
 
 
**About The Company**
Our client is a manufacturer in the Merrimack Valley of Massachusetts that produces high-quality, value-added, hand-crafted products.
 
 
They have roughly 400 employees in the US and a workforce that spans down the East Coast, but the majority of the workforce is in MA.
 
 
**The Opportunity**
The Plant Manager owns the day-to-day performance of the company's Massachusetts production facility, with full accountability for safety, quality, output, cost, and people. This is a hands-on, on-the-floor leadership role in a fast-paced, high-mix, labor-intensive operation.
 
 
The right leader will bring structure and discipline to the plant while keeping the craftsmanship and customer responsiveness that set the business apart. You will partner closely with the executive team, Quality, Continuous Improvement, Sales, and Supply Chain, and you will play a visible role in executing the value creation plan.
 
 
**Key Responsibilities**
**Safety and Operations**

* Lead a strong safety culture with clear accountability, training, and incident prevention; drive OSHA compliance and reduce recordables
* Ensure full compliance with regulations and standards
* Maintain control, sanitation, and traceability standards across all lines

**Operations and Performance**

* Deliver daily, weekly, and monthly production plans that meet customer service, on-time-in-full, and quality targets
* Own plant KPIs, including yield, labor productivity, throughput, OEE, scrap/giveaway, and cost.
* Manage a high-SKU, customized product mix with frequent changeovers and short lead times
* Partner with Supply Chain and Sales on capacity planning, scheduling, and new product launches

**Cost and Financial Management**

* Build and manage the plant operating budget and labor model; identify and deliver cost savings
* Recommend and execute capital projects, including automation and equipment that reduce labor dependency

**Continuous Improvement**

* Embed lean manufacturing tools (5S, standard work, root cause analysis, visual management, tiered daily huddles) in partnership with the Continuous Improvement function
* Use data to identify losses and drive sustainable improvements in yield and efficiency

**People and Culture**

* Lead, develop, and hold accountable a team of supervisors and leads across multiple shifts
* Attract, train, and retain a diverse hourly workforce; build bench strength and succession
* Communicate clearly and visibly on the floor; set a tone of respect, ownership, and teamwork

**Maintenance and Facility**

* Oversee preventive maintenance, equipment reliability, and facility upkeep to minimize downtime

**Qualifications**
**Required**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Operations, Business, or a related field, or equivalent experience
* 8+ years of manufacturing experience, including 3+ years as a Plant Manager, Operations Manager, or Production Manager with full P&L or plant-level accountability
* Proven track record of improving safety, yield, labor productivity, and cost in a high-mix, labor-intensive environment
* Hands-on lean manufacturing or continuous improvement experience
* Ability to work on-site north of Boston, MA

**Preferred**

* Experience in a high-growth company
* Experience introducing automation into a manual or semi-automated operation
* Lean Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt; certification
* Bilingual English/Spanish or experience leading a multilingual workforce

**Leadership Profile and First-Year Success**
**What We're Looking For In The Leader**

* Floor-first: visible, approachable, and present on every shift
* Accountable and data-driven: sets clear expectations and measures results
* A builder of people who develops supervisors into leaders
* Calm and decisive in a fast-moving, customer-driven environment
* Comfortable with the pace and expectations of PE ownership

**What Success Looks Like In The First 12 Months**

* Measurable improvement in safety and performance
* A consistent daily management system with KPI boards and tiered huddles in place
* Documented gains in yield, labor productivity, and on-time delivery
* A stable, engaged supervisory team with reduced hourly turnover
* A prioritized capital and automation roadmap aligned with leadership

records.description:
LHH is seeking a Plant Manager for a Direct Hire, Permanent Placement position with a manufacturing client located near Fort Wayne, IN. This is an opportunity to lead a growing manufacturing operation where you will have significant autonomy and direct influence over business and operational performance. You will join an existing team, provide guidance, drive business growth, and lead critical projects with key customers. The compensation is commensurate to experience and will range between $140,000–165,000 per year plus bonus and includes comprehensive benefit and insurance plans, generous Paid Time Off, and a 401K plan with a company match.

***\*\*\*Must be authorized to work in the U.S. without employer sponsorship.\*\*\****

**JOB RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Provide overall leadership and direction for across the manufacturing facility.
* Build an engaged, accountable culture through visible leadership, open communication, coaching, and employee development.
* Evaluate production performance and operating data to identify opportunities for efficiency, capacity, and cost improvements.
* Lead continuous improvement initiatives that increase productivity, reduce waste, and deliver measurable financial results.
* Manage staffing, training, labor utilization, production schedules, and resources to support changing business requirements.
* Review and improve operating procedures, standard work, and processes to strengthen consistency and accountability.
* Develop operating budgets and manage plant spending with a strong focus on profitability and cost control.
* Lead strategic planning activities and establish performance measures that support key organizational objectives.
* Direct capital investments and special projects from planning through implementation and performance validation.
* Improve equipment reliability, utilization, manufacturing capacity, and overall operational effectiveness.
* Maintain strong customer service while balancing production priorities, operating costs, and delivery expectations.
* Foster collaboration across departments and effectively lead employees with diverse backgrounds, experiences, and personalities.
* Maintain a strong safety culture and ensure operations comply with applicable workplace and regulatory requirements.
* Proactively identify operational risks, develop practical action plans, and follow initiatives through completion.
* Partner with technical and business leaders to support long-term growth and continuous operational improvement.

**QUALIFICATIONS**

* **Bachelor Degree in Engineering, Business Management, Operations, or related field is preferred**
* **Minimum of 10+ years of leadership experience within a manufacturing facility is required**
* **Must have at least 5+ years of experience at the Plant Manager level**
* **Must have the ability to manage P&L, labor costs, scheduling, capacity, and capital expenditures**
* Must have experience with ERP/MRP systems and data-driven operational reporting
* Ideal candidates will have experience with Lean Manufacturing
* Strong communication, analytical, problem-solving, and cross-functional leadership skills.
* **Must be authorized to work in the U.S. without employer sponsorship.**

If you or someone in your network fit this profile and would like to apply for this Plant Manager position near Fort Wayne, IN then please submit your application alongside your resume using the link in this posting.
